after.title: Preprint: Broader functional and memory antibody responses in adult females than males in response to seasonal H3N2 vaccine virus
after.authors: Park, H.-S.; Yin, A.; Parish, M. A.; Hu, J.; Zou, A.; Pandey, R.; Fenstermacher, K. Z. J.; Rothman, R. E.; Pekosz, A.; Toapanta, F. R.; Klein, S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: W. Harry Feinstone Department of Molecular Microbiology and Immunology, Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health
after.abstract: Females of reproductive ages often mount greater antibody responses than males following influenza vaccination, but the breadth and depth of these differences, including antibody-dependent Fc receptor (FcR)-mediated functions have not been explored. Plasma samples were collected from male and female healthcare workers (range of 21-48y; mean of 31y) at 0, 28, and 180 days post-vaccination (DPV) during the 2022-2023 influenza vaccine season to assess antibody responses to A/H1N1, A/H3N2, and B/Victoria vaccine viruses. Females had greater A/H3N2, but not A/H1N1 or B/Victoria, neutralizing antibody (nAb) responses compared to males through 180 DPV, with differences being most pronounced among A/H3N2 responders ([≥]4 fold-change in nAb titers). Memory B cells isolated from female responders secreted more IgG in response to ex vivo H3 stimulation than those from males at 28 and 180 DPV. Before vaccination, female responders had greater anti-H3 IgG responses and Fc{gamma}RIIB (CD32b) antibody binding than males, with females maintaining greater responses through 180 DPV. Female responders had greater H3-specific antibody-dependent monocyte phagocytosis (ADMP) and natural killer cell (ADNK) secretion of IFN{gamma} and CCL4 prior to and after vaccination, with ADMP positively correlating with greater H3N2 neutralization through 180 DPV in females only. Among responders, the durability of ADMP, ADNK, and nAb in females as compared to males defined the sex differences in influenza-vaccine induced immunity. The greater Fc{gamma}R-binding antibodies prior to vaccination in females might improve the durability of both neutralizing and non-neutralizing antibody responses to diverse vaccines, including next generation influenza vaccines.

data.summary: added: Preprint: Does educational attainment change the association between meat intake and obesity? A case-study from urban Brazil.

after.title: Preprint: Does educational attainment change the association between meat intake and obesity? A case-study from urban Brazil.
after.authors: Laurentino, J.; Palmeira, P.; Levasseur, P.
after.abstract: Brazil is one of the higher meat producer and consumer worldwide. Recently, the sustainability of the meat market is questioned on regard to its high contribution to climate change and public health concerns such as obesity. Hence, further public policies are likely to regulate the meat market and simultaneously reduce meat production and consumption. However, in the context of middle-income countries marked by strong inequalities such as Brazil, the nutritional effect of such market regulation is uncertain. Indeed, one can hypothesize that meat intake plays a protective role against poor nutritious food intake and weight gain among underprivileged settings. To test this hypothesis, this study analyzes household cross-sectional yearly surveys collected from 2018 to 2023 in the 27 Brazilian State capitals. As expected, multivariate estimates show education-specific associations between meat intake and obesity. Among the most educated individuals, declaring not consuming any meat the previous day before the survey is associated with lower body mass index (BMI) and obesity risk, as observed in previous epidemiological studies. By contrast, declaring consuming meat the previous day before the survey appears to be protective against weight gain among poorly educated individuals. We also observe education-specific meat substitution behaviors that help explain these findings. In facts, meat is more likely to be replaced by sweets and ready-to-eat meals among poorly educated individuals compared to more educated ones. We conclude that, everything being equals, meat market regulation policy might worsen public health concerns for under-privileged individuals. Important investments in the education sector and anti-poverty programs are thus needed to limit the raise of nutritional inequalities.

after.title: Preprint: Development and Validation of MetaVidence: A No-Code Application for Accessible and Reproducible Meta-analysis
after.authors: FILHO, V. O. C.; Passos, P. R. C.; Noronha, M. M.; Nohmi, R. L.; da Silva, L. F. L.; Saldanha, E. F.; Leite, G. G. F.
after.abstract: BACKGROUND: Meta-analyses are central to evidence-based medicine, but the R packages that implement current methods require programming skills, and most graphical tools cover only a single study design. Here, we aimed to develop and validate a free no-code application that performs the main forms of meta-analysis within a single interface. METHODS: We developed MetaVidence as a Shiny application built on the meta, metafor, netmeta and lme4 packages, which runs in the browser through WebAssembly and is also available as an R package. Agreement with direct package calls was evaluated across effect measures, models, estimators and secondary analyses, and 12 published meta-analyses were reconstructed. Usability was assessed with the System Usability Scale among researchers who had previously conducted a meta-analysis. RESULTS: MetaVidence performs pairwise, single-arm, pre-calculated, network and diagnostic test accuracy meta-analysis through a three-step workflow of data verification, model specification and results. In three of the five families, multiple outcomes can be analyzed in a single run with the same settings, and every analysis reports the parameters that should be described in the methods section. A total of 6,321 validation checks were performed, and the maximum absolute difference in the reference-dataset comparisons was 3.9x10^(-16). The diagnostic module reproduced the anti-CCP example of the Cochrane Handbook to within 0.0002, and all 12 published meta-analyses were reproduced within half of the last reported digit. Fifty-nine researchers rated MetaVidence with a mean System Usability Scale score of 82.8 (95% CI 76.2-89.5). CONCLUSIONS: MetaVidence integrates the main forms of meta-analysis into a single validated interface that does not require programming. These findings support its use as an accessible and reproducible resource for evidence synthesis, particularly for researchers without programming skills or statistical support.

after.title: Preprint: Patient-Expressed Needs, Burdens and Barriers in Taiwanese Online Health Discussions: A Taiwan-Contextualized Friction Framework Applied With Large Language Model-Based Social Listening
after.authors: Liu, Z.-Y.; Chieh, T.; Kuo, C.-F.
after.abstract: Background: Patients' difficulties with illness and care (not understanding a result, distress, daily restrictions, not knowing where to go, family strain) may not surface in clinical encounters or records. Regulatory guidance on patient-focused drug development recognizes social-media listening as a source of patient experience data, but no systematic framework exists for Traditional Chinese discussions in Taiwan, and keyword pipelines measure such content poorly. Objective: To characterize patient-expressed needs, burdens and barriers ("frictions") in Taiwanese online health discussions with an eight-domain, Taiwan-contextualized framework, identify whose frictions they are, and assess how securely each is measured. Methods: From a 13.6-million-unit archive of the PTT forum and three ask-a-physician services, seeded samples of 9,131 pipeline-flagged units and 1,000 unflagged forum articles (10,130 distinct units) were read in full by a large language model under rubrics for relevance, author (patient or family member) and eight domains: information gap, emotional burden, lifestyle burden, medication experience, system navigation, access barrier, caregiver burden and cost burden. Profiles were reported separately for forum articles and physician submissions and checked against a second vendor, two physicians' independent labels of 160 accepted and rejected units, and the archive's keyword pipeline. Results: Among 2,395 model-confirmed forum articles, 83.1% voiced at least one friction: information gap 59.5% (physicians 86%-93%), emotional burden 39.0%, medication experience 24.1%, lifestyle burden 22.2% and system navigation 16.3%; access barrier, caregiver burden and cost burden were each below 7%. Of 3,105 submissions, nearly all were questions and 53.8% also carried a burden. Navigation rarely concerned insurance (9.1%). Family-authored forum articles (14.5%) more often voiced emotional burden (54.9% vs 36.3%), navigation (34.8% vs 13.2%; instrument-dependent) and access barriers (16.4% vs 4.7%), and patient-authored articles lifestyle burden (24.8% vs 6.9%); caregiver burden came with emotional burden in 86.0% of articles voicing it. Emotional and lifestyle burden were commoner in forum articles than submissions under the model, a second vendor and both physicians; medication experience and navigation were instrument-dependent, and physicians disagreed on cost (32% vs 4%). The keyword pipeline had stored its information-gap output for 29.9% of model-confirmed reference-stratum units and over-counted insurance navigation 2.9-fold; its relevance flag was 50.5% precise for forum articles and reached an estimated 42.9% of patient-voice articles. Conclusions: Systematic listening organized Taiwanese patients' and families' online accounts into eight clinically interpretable friction domains, led by the need to understand and by emotional burden, with family-authored posts more often voicing navigation and access difficulty. These expressed concerns may not surface in routine encounters; they identify candidate targets for patient-centred communication and services, which require evaluation. Some domain levels depended on the reader, and keyword pipelines missed or distorted them, so such work needs full-text reading, explicit definitions and clinician checks. Keywords: social media; patient experience data; patient-focused drug development; unmet needs; caregivers; natural language processing; large language models; content analysis; Taiwan; national health insurance

after.title: Preprint: Patient- and Family-Expressed Needs and Burdens in Kidney-Related Online Discussions in Taiwan: Large Language Model-Based Analysis Across Clinical Contexts
after.authors: Liu, Z.-Y.; Hung, Y.-C.; Kuo, C.-F.
after.abstract: Introduction: What people with kidney concerns or disease and their families struggle with between visits may not surface in clinic. We mapped the needs and burdens they express online by clinical context and author. Methods: A large language model read all 22,170 posts reached by a chronic kidney disease tag or kidney lexicon on a Taiwanese forum and 3 ask-a-physician services (1995-2026), applying a companion friction framework with kidney-specific fields, author (patient or family) and clinical context. A second vendor re-read 11,010 posts; 2 physicians labelled relevance, author and context in 200. Results: Among 6,023 kidney-related posts, the reproducibly measured fields most often voiced on the forum were information needs (79%), emotional burden (48%), system navigation (34%) and worry about progression (24%). After abnormal tests, 54%-56% of posts quoted a laboratory value, nearly always with a question or stated uncertainty; renal-diet burden peaked with diagnosed disease; caregiver burden rose to 29% of dialysis-or-transplantation forum posts. Family-written posts more often voiced navigation difficulty and caregiver burden. Most fields agreed with the second vendor (kappa 0.65-0.98). On the model's labels, family members wrote 25% of forum posts about kidney concerns and 74% about dialysis or transplantation; on a 139-post sample, physicians' labels gave 47%-48% for dialysis or transplantation (model 71%). Conclusion: Kidney-related posts carry context-specific information needs and emotional and practical burdens, many voiced by relatives. They suggest candidate responses (test-result explanation, diet support, family-directed information and support) that need evaluation. Keywords: chronic kidney disease; dialysis; patient experience; caregivers; social media; large language models

after.title: Preprint: ClinDataBench: Benchmarking Large Language Model Agents in Clinical Trial Analysis Dataset Construction
after.authors: Li, Z.; Luo, Y.; Feng, Y.; Xu, J.
after.abstract: A new drug reaches patients only after the U.S. Food and Drug Administration (FDA) has reviewed its trial evidence, which every application carries as analysis datasets in the Clinical Data Interchange Standards Consortium (CDISC) Analysis Data Model (ADaM) format that programmers derive by hand from raw trial data, a statistical analysis plan (SAP) and dataset specifications. Coding agents built on large language models (LLMs) could take over this work, and a slow-changing industry will adopt them only with evidence of what they get right and wrong. However, work on large language models (LLMs) for CDISC data stops short of evaluating a complete, conformant and reproducible package, and the standard validator checks structure rather than whether each value is derived correctly. We introduce ClinDataBench, built on the public CDISC pilot study: an agent receives 22 Study Data Tabulation Model (SDTM) domains, the statistical analysis plan (SAP) and specifications, and must deliver 13 Analysis Data Model (ADaM) datasets, Define-XML metadata and a program that rebuilds them offline. Agents run in containers whose only network route is their model API, restricting online access to published reference outputs during execution. A host-only evaluator scores conformance under the Pinnacle 21 Community (P21) validator, selected derivations, clean reconstruction and effort separately. We compare three settings: Base, which submits the agent's first package; Self-Refine, which revises it without external validation feedback; and CRITIC, which revises it with the agent's own validator report. In an exploratory pilot with six models, the three closed models and DeepSeek delivered all 13 datasets in every setting and eleven of their twelve packages rebuilt semantically, while two other open-weight models delivered no complete package. Validator findings ranged from 15 to 64 dataset-rule pairs. Four of six CRITIC workflows had usable validator comparisons, and each reduced its finding count. None reduced its failed derivation count. The package with the fewest findings carried none of the 234 efficacy summary records in the form the specifications define, showing that lower validator finding counts do not necessarily indicate more correct derivations.

after.title: Preprint: Assessing the Perception of Usefulness and Use of Syndromic Surveillance of Surgical Site Infections for Improvement of Infection Prevention and Control in Health Facilities of Tanzania: A Qualitative Design for Publication
after.authors: Hokororo, J. C.
after.author_corresponding_institution: United Republic of Tanzania Ministry of Health
after.abstract: Tanzania has recently set up a syndromic surveillance of Surgical Site Infections (SSIs) system with the aim to determine the burden of SSI in the country. This study Assessed the Use and Usefulness of it for Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) improvement in health facilities of Tanzania. The study utilized the classic Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) adapted specifically for healthcare information systems; the research team developed semi-structured Key Informants Interview (KII) guides. The QIT members were purposefully selected as KIIs in PHFs. Data collection continued until saturation was achieved, ultimately gathering insights from a total of 49 participants across 20 PHFs in Tanzania from September to November 2025. The interviews were audio-recorded and lasted for around 60 minutes. Privacy was ensured by conducting the interview in an isolated room. Textual data were coded and categorized using NVivo version 20.2 (NVivo.exe). The QIT members reported their perception that syndromic surveillance helped to track SSIs, helped to get burden and trends, and were useful for planning. Participants generally liked the syndromic surveillance and reported using them to inform program design, guide development of intervention and enhance personal knowledge. The participants shared important feedback to improve the syndromic surveillance, particularly as a need to enhance improvement of IPC. Tanzanias syndromic surveillance system use for tracking SSIs in primary care is recognized by QIT as a transformative tool for mapping SSI burdens and informing strategic planning. To ensure long term success, stakeholders must address feedback by strengthening quality of data, providing continuous training, and adapting the system to meet local needs. The overall results of this study showed the importance of conducting syndromic surveillance in order to understand the burden of SSI so as to come up with mitigation strategies of improving IPC across the health system.

This study Assessed the Use and Usefulness of it for Infection Prevention and Control (IPC) improvement in health facilities of Tanzania. The study utilized the classic Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) adapted specifically for healthcare information systems; the research team developed semi-structured Key Informants Interview (KII) guides. The QIT members were purposefully selected as KIIs in PHFs. Data collection continued until saturation was achieved, ultimately gathering insights from a total of 49 participants across 20 PHFs in Tanzania from September to November 2025. The interviews were audio-recorded and lasted for around 60 minutes. Privacy was ensured by conducting the interview in an isolated room. Textual data were coded and categorized using NVivo version 20.2 (NVivo.exe). To ensure long term success, stakeholders must address feedback by strengthening quality of data, providing continuous training, and adapting the system to meet local needs. after.abstract: Acute myeloid leukemia (AML) is clinically and genetically heterogeneous. Current risk stratification systems based on cytogenetic and genetic abnormalities do not fully capture prognostic heterogeneity, particularly among intermediate-risk patients. Long non-coding RNAs (lncRNAs) have emerged as key regulators of AML biology, contributing to leukemogenesis, impaired differentiation, apoptosis resistance, and treatment response. In this study, we developed we developed a bone marrow-derived lncRNA prognostic signature, termed lncSigAML, using in pediatric samples from TARGET-AML (n = 1,594) and validated it in four bone marrow and peripheral blood datasets from TARGET-AML, Beat AML, and TCGA-LAML (n = 1,087). Ten lncRNAs were selected: MEF2C-AS1, LINC00477, PROSER2-AS1, LINC01122, KCNJ2-AS1, LINC01108, AP001042.1, SOCS2-AS1, ST3GAL6-AS1, and LINC00355. Among candidate models, random survival forest achieved the best performance and significantly stratified patients into high- and low-risk groups (cross-validated HR = 2.87, 95%CI: 2.43-3.4; P < 0.001) in TARGET-AML bone marrow samples, with stable prognostic performance over 1-, 3-, and 5- year follow-up. The lncSigAML signature also robustly demonstrates significant prognostic effects across all cross-cohort and cross-tissue datasets separately (pooled HR = 2.91; 95%CI = 2.31-3.68; P <0.001). Meta-analysis showed substantially higher pooled 1-, 3-, and 5-year overall survival in the low-risk group than in the high-risk group (80.5%, 63.4%, and 55.3% vs. 52.1%, 28.1%, and 23.9%, respectively). Multivariable Cox regression demonstrated that lncSigAML provided prognostic information beyond clinical variables, genetic subtypes, and cytogenetic risk, with significant incremental prognostic value by partial likelihood ratio testing. Pathway analysis showed enrichment of genes related to cell survival and proliferation, impaired immune surveillance, and aggressive AML biology in the high-risk group, including STK33-, IL2-, and PTEN-associated pathways. To support clinical and research applications, we implemented lncSigAML as an interactive, publicly accessible web application for individualized prognostic estimation. Prospective validation and functional studies of the identified lncRNAs will further evaluate their potential utility in precision AML care.

after.authors: Long, L.; Brown, B.; Hugo, J.; Bokolo, S.; Hendrickson, C.; Pettinato, C.; Gupta, S.; Lakay, I.; Nkaphe, M.; Thirumurthy, H.; Fox, M. P.; McIntyre, J.

after.abstract: Background. Oral pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) is highly effective for preventing HIV acquisition when used consistently, but uptake and persistence remain suboptimal among gay men and other men who have sex with men (MSM) in South Africa. We examined client and provider perspectives on PrEP uptake and persistence. Methods. Between September and December 2022, we conducted three focus group discussions with 16 HIV-negative MSM eligible for, but not using, PrEP and six key informant interviews with PrEP providers at a specialized key population health clinic in Cape Town, South Africa. We analyzed transcripts thematically, using deductive codes informed by the PrEP cascade and the COM-B (capability, opportunity, motivation) model, plus inductive codes for emerging issues. Results. Five themes emerged. Limited knowledge, misconceptions about PrEP and antiretroviral therapy, and low perceived risk reduced clients capability to make informed decisions about PrEP. HIV- and sexuality-related stigma, concerns about disclosure, and social surveillance were socially costly. Distance, transport costs, work commitments, clinic hours, and visit burden limited physical opportunity, whereas free care, short visits, reminders, and multi-month dispensing facilitated access. Daily pill-taking, side effects, forgetfulness, and changing sexual activity complicated persistence; routines, reminders, and acceptable PrEP modalities supported continued use. Non-judgmental, MSM-affirming services, counseling, and trusted providers fostered motivation by strengthening clients sense of safety, agency, and control. Conclusion. PrEP delivery for MSM should extend beyond medication provision and address knowledge, stigma, service convenience, and motivation. Low-intensity adaptations, including tailored counseling, affirming care, flexible multi-month dispensing, and reminders, may improve uptake and persistence.

after.authors: Lo Hog Tian, J. M.; Atkins, K.; Murray, S. M.; Glick, J. L.; Lucas, I. L.; Valentine-Graves, M.; Winter, S.; Caldwell, J. A.; Sanchez, T.; Baral, S. D.; Wiginton, J. M.

after.abstract: Introduction Transgender women experience stigma related to both gender identity and sexual behavior, yet robust measurement tools remain limited. This study evaluated the factor structure and external construct validity of the Measures of Attributional Stigma for gender identity (MAS-GI) and sexual behavior (MAS-SB) among transgender women in the United States. Methods We analyzed cross-sectional data from the Transgender Womens Internet Survey and Testing (TWIST) platform collected from 2023-2025 (N=2,901). Participants completed parallel 14-item stigma measures attributed separately to gender identity and sexual behavior. The sample was split into exploratory factor analysis (EFA; n=1,951; 2023-2024) and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA; n=950; 2024-2025) samples. External construct validity was evaluated via associations with depression symptoms, posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD), social capital, transgender identity pride, and healthcare utilization. Results EFA identified three MAS-GI factors (family stigma, anticipated healthcare stigma, and enacted social stigma) and two MAS-SB factors (global healthcare stigma and social/institutional stigma). CFA confirmed both structures with good to excellent model fit. All stigma dimensions were positively associated with depression and PTSD. Anticipated healthcare and enacted social stigma from the MAS-GI and both MAS-SB dimensions were negatively associated with social capital. Greater anticipated gender identity healthcare stigma associated with lower transgender identity pride. Several stigma dimensions were also positively associated with HIV/STI testing, PrEP use, and mental healthcare utilization. Conclusions The MAS-GI and MAS-SB demonstrate factorial validity and preliminary external construct validity among transgender women. These measures enable precise assessment of stigma by attribution and source and inform stigma surveillance and intervention evaluation.

after.authors: Mecha, J. O.; Muhua, G. O.; Githua, J.; N. Escudero, J.; Kijaro, L.; N. Njagi, L.; John-Stewart, G.; Maleche-Obimbo, E.; Nduba, V.; M. LaCourse, S.; Y.T. Inoue, L.
after.abstract: Background: Pediatric tuberculosis (TB) remains difficult to diagnose. Culture, the gold standard, has limited sensitivity in children (~40-60%). We analyzed 452 symptomatic children [≤]15 years who underwent chest x-ray (CXR), respiratory sample testing with Xpert Ultra, smear microscopy and culture, tuberculin skin test (TST), and interferon gamma release assay (IGRA) in Nairobi, Kenya. Methods: Three Bayesian latent class models (BLCMs) were used: Model 1 assumed conditional test independence; Model 2 incorporated random effects to account for shared biological (Smear, geneXpert Ultra/RIF and culture) or immunologic (IGRA, TST) test dependence; Model 3 extended Model 2 by adjusting for clinical covariates and NIH TB signs and symptoms. We estimated TB prevalence, test sensitivities/specificities and covariate effects. Results: Prevalence estimates under Models 1 [20.2% (15.9-24.7)] and 2 [24.5% (19.6-30.0)] were higher than under Model 3 [14.8% (11.0-19.3)]. All the three model-based prevalence estimates were considerably higher than the 9.9% of children identified through microbiological testing alone. Sensitivity and specificity were broadly consistent across models. Model 3 was considered preferred because it accounted for dependence among the tests and adjusted prevalence and sensitivity for clinical covariates. Under this Model 3, culture and GeneXpert MTB/RIF Ultra demonstrated moderate sensitivity (56.9% and 63.2%, respectively), while smear microscopy showed lower sensitivity (29.8%). CXR achieved moderate sensitivity (79.7%) but limited specificity (40.2%). IGRA and TST displayed sensitivities of 63.7% and 50.1%, and specificities of 81.5% and 65.8%. Older age was positively associated with TB (log-odds ratio 1.09; 95% CrI: 0.14-2.18).   Conclusion: BLCMs estimated TB prevalence and test accuracies without a gold standard. Sensitivity analyses confirmed robustness to priors. Radiography demonstrated moderate sensitivity while culture and GeneXpert retained excellent specificity with improved test performance with older age.

after.authors: Koross, A. K.; Shisanya, M. S.; Kandagor, E.; Kosgei, D.; Jepkosgei, V.
after.abstract: Cyberbullying research is constrained by inconsistent measurement, and the instruments most widely used were developed and validated in European and Asian school samples rather than in African higher-education settings. This study evaluated the factor structure, reliability, construct validity and sex measurement invariance of a 22-item measure of cybervictimisation and cyberperpetration based on the European Cyberbullying Intervention Project Questionnaire among health-professions students in Kenya. In a multicampus cross-sectional survey conducted between September and November 2025, 406 students (215 women, 191 men) enrolled at Kenya Medical Training College campuses completed 11 victimisation and 11 perpetration items together with measures of depression, anxiety and stress symptoms, problematic social-media use, self-esteem and well-being. Items were modelled as ordered categorical indicators by confirmatory factor analysis with the WLSMV estimator. A one-factor model was compared with a correlated two-factor model; reliability was estimated using ordinal alpha, McDonald's omega and composite reliability; convergent validity used Spearman correlations with bootstrap intervals and Holm adjustment; and invariance across sex was tested sequentially. Every item showed a pronounced floor effect. The correlated two-factor model fitted markedly better than the one-factor model (scaled difference {chi}{superscript 2}(1) = 48.06, p < .001) and, after three content-matched residual covariances were released, fitted the data well (CFI = .984, TLI = .982, RMSEA = .049, 90% CI .042 to .056, SRMR = .044). Standardised loadings ranged from .627 to .928, and the latent correlation between dimensions was .849 (95% CI .803 to .895). Omega was .951 for cybervictimisation and .975 for cyberperpetration. Both dimensions correlated positively with distress and problematic social-media use and negatively with self-esteem, but showed negligible correlations with well-being. Configural, threshold and loading invariance across sex were supported. The findings support scoring the instrument as two reliable, sex-comparable but strongly overlapping dimensions.

after.authors: Kariuki, T.; Kariuki, J.; Mogere, D.; Onyancha, J.; Moriasi, G.
after.abstract: Girls who become pregnant during adolescence in sub-Saharan Africa carry a high burden of depressive symptoms. Kenyan studies have relied on antenatal clinic samples and have not looked at stigma, the response to pregnancy disclosure and economic circumstances in the same analysis. We assessed how these factors relate to depressive symptom burden among adolescent mothers in Juja Sub-County, Kiambu County. We surveyed 227 girls who had been pregnant or given birth at 10-19 years, drawn by stratified random sampling from a line list of 466 mapped across five wards. Trained assistants administered a structured questionnaire covering background characteristics, pregnancy and disclosure, stigma, and a seven-item depressive symptom checklist. Elevated symptom burden was set in advance at four or more endorsed items. Two logistic regression models examined factors linked to stigma (n = 199) and to elevated symptom burden (n = 184). Of those with parity data, 194 of 197 had already given birth. Most respondents were 17-19 years old (86.8%) and single (69.2%), 92.5% had no income of their own, and 47.1% had left school early. Nine in ten pregnancies (91.2%) were unplanned, and 41.4% of girls met anger, rejection or indifference when they first disclosed. Stigma was reported by 43.2%, elevated symptom burden by 27.1% and thoughts of self-harm by 16.4%. Only 27.3% had attended any support programme. Being single was the one factor associated with stigma (adjusted odds ratio [AOR] 3.50; 95% confidence interval [CI] 1.48-8.31). Elevated symptom burden was associated with stigma (AOR 3.21; 1.54-6.69) and with an unsupportive disclosure reaction (AOR 2.54; 1.19-5.41), and was less likely with each additional year of age (AOR 0.69; 0.49-0.96). Programme attendance showed no association (AOR 0.89; 0.41-1.94). In this peri-urban community, depressive symptoms clustered among adolescent mothers who had been stigmatised or poorly received when they disclosed their pregnancy, and stigma tracked marital status more closely than poverty. Screening with validated tools at postnatal, child-health and antenatal visits, guidance for families and partners on responding to disclosure, and community work on attitudes to unmarried motherhood deserve testing in this setting.

after.abstract: Purpose - This study examines whether six health behaviors remain stable among high school students across the school year and whether associations between these behaviors recur across assessments. Design/methodology/approach - As part of a school health program evaluation, a pre-post longitudinal health survey was conducted among two samples of high school students in a U.S. vocational-technical high school. Study 1 surveyed 114 students from late winter to late spring in 2024. Study 2 surveyed 177 students from autumn 2024 to late spring 2025. Wilcoxon signed-rank tests examined group-level behavioral change, and Pearson correlation networks described associations among six health behaviors: sleep, breakfast consumption, physical activity, nature exposure, social media use, and mindfulness practices. Findings - The primary analyses detected no significant group-level changes in any of the six behaviors across either study interval, suggesting relative stability within these samples. A one-time survey may provide useful information for broad school health planning, whereas repeated assessment remains necessary for evaluating longer-term patterns or program effects. Sleep and breakfast showed the most consistent positive association. Physical activity and nature exposure were positively associated at three of the four assessments. Social media was isolated from the other behaviors at the first three assessments but was negatively associated with sleep and physical activity at the final assessment. Originality - The study distinguishes stability in group-level behavior from changes in the relationships among behaviors. The findings support efficient assessment for broad educational planning. They also identify behavior pairs that can be addressed together in school health education, including sleep and breakfast, physical activity and nature exposure, and social media, sleep, and physical activity.

after.title: Preprint: Automated Gland MRI Radiomics for Predicting Time to Pathologic Progression during Prostate Cancer Active Surveillance
after.authors: Zeng, H.; Athreya, S.; Dai, D.; Pleasure, M.; Ivezic, V.; Raman, S.; Marks, L.; Speier, W.; Arnold, C.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Radiological Sciences, University of California, Los Angeles
after.abstract: Background: Repeated biopsies burden patients during prostate cancer active surveillance (AS). Existing MRI risk stratification tools avoiding biopsy remain limited by the difficulty of automated lesion segmentation. Purpose: To develop a model integrating gland MRI radiomics and clinicopathologic variables for predicting time to pathologic progression during prostate cancer AS. Materials and Methods: This retrospective single-institution study included men with grade group 1 or favorable grade group 2 prostate cancer undergoing AS with fusion-targeted and systematic biopsy (2010-2025). Gland segmentation used nnU-Net; gland radiomic features were selected by LASSO-penalized survival regression to train an XGBoost accelerated failure time model. Comparator models were assessed by C-index, time-dependent area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC), Kaplan-Meier, and decision curve analysis. Results: Of 522 men (median age, 64 years [IQR, 59-68]), 410 were assigned by site to development and 112 to internal testing. Gland segmentation Dice was 0.89 +/- 0.04. The C-index was higher for the gland radiomics model (0.77) than for clinicopathologic (0.68) and lesion radiomics (0.68) models (adjusted P [≤] .017), with the highest time-dependent AUC at 36 months (0.87 [95% CI: 0.78, 0.94]). Progression-free survival was lower in high-risk than low-risk groups (36 months, 63.9% vs 100%; 48 months, 55.4% vs 93.8%; log-rank P < .001). At a 0.25 risk threshold, 49.1% and 31.3% were low risk at 36 and 48 months (negative predictive value, 1.00; positive predictive value, 0.36). Conclusion: An automated gland radiomics model predicted time to pathologic progression during AS better than clinicopathologic and lesion-based models.

after.authors: fukui, y.; higashiyama, s.; kawata, y.; nagatani, y.; iguchi, h.; watanabe, y.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Radiology, Shiga University of Medical Science Hospital
after.abstract: Purpose: To compare fine-tuned encoders, generative large language models (LLMs) and typed decisions (per-finding yes/no questions answered with a probability) for classifying 18 findings in chest CT reports, and to identify when typed decisions help. Methods: This retrospective study used public data. The internal test set comprised 150 CT-RATE reports with paired Japanese translations at three quality levels; the external test set, 243 naturally written Japanese reports with human annotations (RR-Findings). We compared ModernBERT encoders fine-tuned on 20,444 reports, generative LLMs (gpt-6-luna, Qwen3.8-27B, MedGemma), and typed decisions with Jev, the Decisions API and Qwen. Thresholds fixed on 450 development reports were applied unchanged externally. The primary metric was micro-F1; case-level paired bootstrap 95% confidence intervals (CIs) were calculated for 11 internal comparisons. Results: Encoders were best internally (English 0.9853; radiologist-checked Japanese 0.9576) and exceeded Jev (differences 0.0367, 95% CI 0.0258-0.0484; 0.0336, 0.0215-0.0464). Externally, Jev (0.8844) lay within the encoder seed range (0.8656-0.9144), exceeded the three generative conditions tested externally (best 0.8564) and the Decisions API (0.8177), and had the smallest internal-to-external decrease (-0.0396). An encoder trained on 2,044 reports reached 0.8226 externally. Typed-versus-generated differences changed direction across models and test sets. At a fixed threshold of 0.5, Jev fell to 0.7753 externally. Conclusion: Fine-tuned encoders performed best with ample in-distribution labels. Although threshold-dependent, Jev, with thresholds fitted on only 450 labeled reports, fell within the encoder seed range externally and exceeded the generative LLMs and an encoder trained on 2,044 reports, making it an option when labels are scarce.

after.authors: Alemu, L. A.; Meles, H. N.; Shishay, T.; Berhe, A. K.; Gebregergis, M. W.; Gebregziabiher, B.; Tesfau, Y. B.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Adigrat University College of Medicine and Health Sciences
after.abstract: Background: Poor adherence to Iron and folic acid (IFA) remains major public health challenge in Ethiopia. While national protocols advise IFA supplementation during pregnancy, adherence is low in the nation particularly in rural areas. In the study setting, there is lack of updated data regarding adherence to IFA and its determinant factors among pregnant women. Objective: To assess adherence to IFA supplements and associated factors among pregnant women in rural setting of Eastern Tigray, Ethiopia, 2025. Methods: A community-based cross-sectional study was carried out from March 2025 to April 2025 among 614 pregnant women in Eastern Tigray, Ethiopia. Simple random and systematic random sampling techniques were utilized to select districts and study participants respectively.  Data analysis was performed using SPSS 25, employing both binary and multivariable logistic regression. Multi-collinearity and goodness of fit tests were ensured using the variance inflation factor and Hosmer-Lemeshow test respectively. Statistical significance was declared at a p-value less than 0.05. Results:  A total of 599 participants were included and the prevalence of adherence to IFA Supplementation (IFAS) was 56% (95% CI: 52%, 60%). Having [≥] 4 ANC visits (AOR= 37.7 95% CI: 14.08 - 101.03), mothers with previous history of anemia (AOR=2.2 CI: 1.07 - 4.69), age of mothers [≥] 40 years (AOR= 11.5 CI: 1.06 - 124.05), mothers who received counseling about IFAS (AOR, 7.1; CI 3.24 - 15.37), and mothers travelled to the health facility 30 to 60 minutes and more than 60 minutes (AOR, 0.02; CI 0.01 - 0.04), and (AOR, 0.01(0 - 0.004), respectively had statistically significant association with adherence to IFAS. Conclusion: Women having four or more ANC visits, a previous history of anaemia, receiving counselling about IFAS, older age, and travelling less than 60 minutes to seek healthcare were associated with increased odds of adherence to IFAS.

after.authors: Altman, G. N.; Marti-Trujillo, A.; Hesson, L. B.; Bell, D. A.; Hooper, A. J.; Sharp, A. J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Icahn School of Medicine at Mount Sinai
after.abstract: Background/Objectives: Familial hypercholesterolemia (FH) is a widely prevalent inherited disorder defined by chronically high LDL-C concentrations and a significantly increased risk of cardiovascular disease. While FH is primarily an autosomal dominant disease caused by pathogenic mutations in LDLR, APOB, or PCSK9, approximately 20-60% of clinically diagnosed patients are mutation-negative. A previous survey of over 23,000 methylation profiles identified a differentially methylated region in the promoter of LDLR. This study aimed to investigate whether constitutional hypermethylation of the LDLR promoter is a recurrent cause of FH in patients lacking identifiable pathogenic variants. Methods: We screened 308 mutation-negative clinically confirmed FH patients for promoter hypermethylation in LDLR. We used Combined Bisulfite Restriction Analysis (COBRA) with genomic DNA from peripheral blood samples. The assay assessed methylation at TaqI sites within a 332 bp region of the LDLR promoter. Results: No instances of LDLR promoter hypermethylation were detected among the 308 mutation-negative FH patients. Statistical analysis yielded an upper bound of 1.19% (95% Clopper-Pearson CI) for the prevalence of this specific epimutation in our cohort. Conclusions: Our results indicate that LDLR promoter hypermethylation at this specific locus is not a common cause of the FH phenotype in mutation-negative patients. These findings imply that while methylation in this region may be rare or not significantly contribute to the disease phenotype, the diagnostic gap in FH may be explained by other factors, such as methylation in other regions, polygenic risk, structural variants, or non-canonical regulatory mutations.

after.authors: Riddick, C. C.; Tamaki, C.
after.abstract: Background Deaf older adults are at a heightened risk for falling, yet no fall-reduction programs for Deaf persons have been reported. Culturally responsive balance enhancement programs targeting this underserved population are needed. Consequently, the purposes of the study were to develop and pilot an exercise program for older adults who are Deaf and use American Sign Language (ASL). Methods During a two-year period, 40 community-dwelling Deaf adults (25 women, 15 men; ages 62-92 years) attended two 2-hour classes each week for eight weeks on a college campus, delivered entirely in ASL, with an additional expectation to engage in exercises outside of class. Outcome measures completed at pre- and post-intervention were timed up-and-go (TUG), sit-to-stand (STS), chair sit and reach (SR), Activities-specific Balance Confidence (ABC), and Fall Risk Questionnaire (FRQ). Theoretical frameworks shaped the content and delivery of BIM. Results 67.5% of participants attended [≥]14 classes. Paired-samples t-tests revealed significant improvements in TUG, STS, and SR. Participants who entered the program with an ABC score below 90% experienced substantial improvement, while score changes on the FRQ were not statistically significant even among the at-risk group. Eight adverse events (seven falls) occurred in class, with no serious consequences. Conclusion The culturally responsive BIM engaged participants effectively and led to significant improvements across multiple measures of dynamic balance. Given the high rates of vestibular and lower body weakness among Deaf older adults, vigilant management of fall risks is needed for future class offerings.

after.title: Preprint: Simulation and temporal validation of ICU trajectories after stroke: patient condition, transfer readiness and actual ICU exit
after.authors: LEI, P.; XU, Y.; ZHANG, Y.; Ray, N.; GAO, Y.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Institute of Global Health, Faculty of Medicine, University of Geneva, Geneva, Switzerland; Overseas Liaison Department, School of Public Health, Fudan Universi
after.abstract: Objective: To describe how intensive care unit (ICU) time is composed after stroke, and to test whether simulating patient condition, transfer readiness and ICU exit separately predicts as accurately as direct models. Materials and Methods: In 6,366 ICU stays for stroke in MIMIC IV, hourly readiness criteria divided ICU hours into organ support needs, stroke specific needs, and time not explained by these needs. An hourly simulator was built on stays up to 2016, frozen, and validated on 2017 to 2019 (n=1,714) and 2020 onwards (n=1,521). The primary measure was the 24 hour alive exit Brier score versus the strongest direct model (gradient boosting). Results: Unexplained time was 34.1% of hours in standard ICUs and 87.6% in neuro intermediate units. 37.8% of stays lost readiness for [≥]6 consecutive hours after first confirmation. The simulator and gradient boosting were indistinguishable (Brier 0.1238 vs 0.1245; difference -0.0007, 95% CI -0.0030 to 0.0016). The simulator was better calibrated at 48 and 72 hours but discriminated less well (C statistic 0.71 vs 0.74 to 0.75). All models overpredicted exit after 2016; the error lay mainly after readiness (median 40 hours simulated vs 68 observed). Discussion: Readiness was not a single event: patients often lost and regained it, and many stayed long after meeting it, especially in neuro intermediate units, which exist for monitoring. Separate modelling did not improve accuracy but placed the post 2016 error after readiness, as the unit mix changed. Conclusion: The simulator matched the strongest direct model while also generating complete trajectories. It needs external validation before any clinical use.

after.authors: Ehmen, C.; Ferraz, R.; Blessmann, J.; Sopraseuth, V.; Keoviengkhone, L.; Bispo, A.; Levy, F.; Demchyshyna, I.; Papa, A.; Jelovsek, M.; Korva, M.; Matthies, L.; Ramharter, M.; Nordmann, T.; Gabriel, M.; Günther, S.; Kann, S.; von Possel, R.; Liu, Y.; Schmitz, H.; Schmidt-Chanasit, J.; Emmerich, P.; Deschermeier, C.
after.abstract: Background: Due to extensive antibody cross-reactivity, serological discrimination of IgG antibodies elicited by exposure to different flaviviruses remains challenging. We aimed to develop and validate highly discriminative IgG ELISAs employing an Fc{gamma} receptor (Fc{gamma}R) capture platform and recombinant competitor molecules to suppress cross-reactive responses. Methods: IgG ELISAs targeting Dengue virus (DENV), Zika virus (ZIKV), and West Nile virus (WNV) were established using immobilized human Fc{gamma}RIIA for antibody capture and soluble, labeled nonstructural protein 1 (NS1) as antigen. To suppress flavivirus cross-reactivity, target-specific competitor molecule formulations (Specificity Enhancers (SEs)), comprising unlabeled heterologous NS1 proteins, were incorporated. ELISAs were validated using comprehensive serum panels from Europe, Asia, Africa, and the Americas. Results: Validation revealed reliable detection of seroconversion following DENV, ZIKV, and WNV infections, as well as DENV vaccination. In sera from flavivirus-endemic regions, substantial cross-reactivity was observed in the absence of SEs, predominantly in samples showing strong reactivity to the corresponding homologous antigen. Addition of SEs significantly improved specificity without compromising sensitivity in most sample panels. In complex exposure settings, analysis of differential signal modulation by individual SE components may provide insights into possible exposure histories. Notably, serological discrimination between IgG antibodies elicited by exposure to different WNV lineages could be achieved by combining lineage-homologous NS1 antigens with lineage-heterologous competitor molecules. Conclusions: The flavivirus (NS1) IgG Fc{gamma}R SE ELISA platform enables enhanced differentiation of flavivirus-specific IgG responses in epidemiologically complex settings. Its modular design allows versatile adaptation to newly emerging flaviviruses and supports high-resolution seroepidemiological investigations in One Health contexts.

after.title: Preprint: # Treatment- and tissue-context-specific isotope labeling patterns in patient-derived lung cancer tissues: an independent reanalysis of public metabolomics data
after.authors: Shang, Z.; Geng, H.
after.abstract: Publicly deposited stable-isotope-resolved metabolomics data can be reanalyzed independently, but small patient-derived experiments may produce treatment effects with limited statistical resolution. We reanalyzed a public isotope-resolved metabolomics dataset from patient-derived lung cancer tissue cultures to quantify treatment- and tissue-specific labeling patterns and their uncertainty. We used 38 tissue samples from two patients: matched tumor and non-tumor slices from UK131 treated with vehicle or pembrolizumab and traced with U-13C6-glucose or U-13C5,15N2-glutamine (n = 3 per cell), and a pembrolizumab x WGP {beta}-glucan factorial experiment in UK2035 tumor tissue (n = 3/3/3/2). We recomputed protein-normalized pools, isotopologue distributions, atom-percent excess and pathway summaries. Effects were estimated with log2-scale linear models, Hedges' g, and exact randomization tests that enumerated all assignments compatible with each design; Benjamini-Hochberg q values were calculated within endpoint families. Sixteen macrophage samples were examined only descriptively. In UK131 tumor tissue, labeled non-oxidative pentose phosphate pathway intermediates increased 1.84-fold (model P = 0.036; exact tumor P = 0.10; exact interaction P = 0.16; q = 0.32). Weighted isotopic scrambling increased 1.31-fold (exact interaction P = 0.04; q = 0.20), and glutamine-derived glutathione diversion increased 1.66-fold (exact interaction P = 0.09; q = 0.22). In UK2035, the combination increased the labeled IMP/(ATP+GTP+UTP) ratio 3.64-fold (model interaction P = 3.2 x 10-4; exact P = 0.016; q = 0.097). No endpoint survived Benjamini-Hochberg correction at q < 0.05 in the exact analyses. The reanalysis reproduced the direction of the source study's principal labeling patterns but showed that their statistical support is weaker than model-based P values imply. These results should be treated as hypothesis-generating estimates for larger patient-derived studies, not as evidence of a validated metabolic bottleneck.

after.title: Preprint: Perinatal suicide risk factors: A network analysis
after.authors: Zivin, K.; Zhong, C.; Kahsay, E.; Johns, L.; Spring, E.; Courant, A.; Mezuk, B.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Michigan School of Public Health
after.abstract: Purpose Suicide during pregnancy or after birth (the perinatal period) represents a leading, preventable cause of United States maternal deaths. This study aimed to understand the complex relationship between perinatal status and life circumstances among perinatal suicide decedents in the United States and generate insights regarding suicide risk. Methods This cross-sectional study used decedent data from the 2003-2023 National Violent Death Reporting System suicide mortality registry (N=20,217). We applied psychometric network analysis using 18 binary life circumstances indicators representing four domains: relationships, health, socioeconomic status, and risk factors for suicide. We generated two networks for the overall sample and perinatal sample and assessed network structure, bridge centralities, and stability. Results The analytic sample included 1,297 perinatal and 18,920 non-perinatal decedents. The network of the overall sample was stable. Perinatal status did not appear at the center of the network but connected primarily with intimate partner problems. The network of the perinatal sample was modestly stable. Postpartum status was not at the center of the network but connected to depressed mood and mental health diagnoses. In both networks, depressed mood had the highest bridge betweenness, and there was a consistent link between physical health domains and socioeconomic domains. Conclusion Suicide prevention strategies targeting childbearing-aged women should incorporate factors beyond pregnancy, including physical health, intimate partner relationships, and socioeconomic challenges.

data.summary: added: Preprint: Analysing Spatial and Temporal Concept Drift in Forecasting Malnutrition Admissions in Kenya

after.title: Preprint: Analysing Spatial and Temporal Concept Drift in Forecasting Malnutrition Admissions in Kenya
after.authors: Squires, S.; Chugh, T.; Economou, T.; Hailey, P.; Fortnam, M.
after.abstract: Forecasting malnutrition admissions could support anticipatory planning in health systems, but existing machine learning and statistical approaches have struggled to produce forecasts of practical value. We investigate whether this disappointing performance is partly attributable to spatial and temporal concept drift, whereby relationships between predictors and admissions differ by location and over time, respectively. We also examine whether adaptations to the modelling approach can mitigate these effects. We used malnutrition admissions from 44 subcounties across 14 counties in Kenya between 2015 and 2020, alongside potential predictors including normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI) and rainfall. We conducted univariate, multivariate, and non-linear analyses of spatial and temporal concept drift, and then trained machine learning (ML) forecasting models using adaptations intended to mitigate these drifts. We find substantial spatial and temporal variation in relationships between predictors and admissions. For temporal concept drift in one subcounty the maximum correlation between admissions and time-lagged admissions for different time periods ranged from -0.39 (95% CIs: -0.74 to -0.04) to 0.45 (95% CIs: 0.11 to 0.79); the equivalents for changes between subcounties ranged from a minimum to maximum of -0.18 (95% CIs: -0.45 to 0.09) to 0.64 (95% CIs: 0.43 to 0.85). For non-linear models, there are also substantial changes in feature importance. At a forecast horizon of three months, our best-performing ML model produced a root mean squared error of 1.07 (95% CIs: 0.96 to 1.18), significantly outperforming the best baseline of 1.23 (95% CIs: 1.10 to 1.39); however, the predictions are unlikely to be sufficiently accurate for practical use. These findings suggest that spatial and temporal concept drift should be explicitly considered when developing forecasting models for malnutrition admissions, rather than relying directly on off-the-shelf ML approaches.

after.abstract: Endoglin is a transmembrane glycoprotein that plays a key role in vascular development, angiogenesis and endothelial homeostasis. Its soluble form (Sol-ENG), generated through proteolytic shedding of the membrane-bound protein, has been implicated in the pathophysiology of numerous cardiovascular diseases, ranging from common conditions such as preeclampsia and thrombosis to rare diseases such as hereditary hemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT). Leveraging large-scale genomics, transcriptomics, proteomics and metabolomics data from public and original resources, we identify a molecular signature of 24 markers associated with plasma levels of Sol-ENG. This signature was enriched in genes coding for GPI-enchored proteins and included metabolites participating to glycosylation and redox homeostasis. Furthermore, we observed that ABO blood groups and genetically predicted plasma levels of 5-Azacytidine Induced 2 (AZI2) associate with the risk of arteriovenous malformations in HHT patients. This study provides new insights into the physiological mechanisms underlying Endoglin regulation and opens clinical perspectives for the management of HHT patients.

after.authors: Hansen, P.; Nygaard, H.; Kamper, R. S.; Schultz, M.; Ryg, J.; Aagaard, P.; Dela, F.; Suetta, C.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Copenhagen University Hospital, Bispebjerg and Frederiksberg
after.abstract: Abstract Background: Sarcopenia and frailty pose considerable risks to older adults due to their close association with reduced physical performance, increased risks of falls, and mortality. Despite this, knowledge about the prevalence in mobility-limited older adults remains scarce. Therefore, we aimed to identify the prevalence and co-prevalence of sarcopenia and frailty in mobility-limited older adults. Methods: This cross-sectional study included patients aged [≥]65 years referred to a geriatric outpatient clinic for fall assessment. Sarcopenia risk was screened using SARC-F and defined according to the European Working Group on Sarcopenia in Older People criteria; frailty was evaluated using the Clinical Frailty Scale. Muscle strength was assessed by handgrip strength and the 30-second sit-to-stand test. Skeletal muscle index was determined using bioelectrical impedance analysis (Inbody770). Gait speed was assessed over 6 meters. Results: A total of 375 patients (mean age 79.7 {+/-} 6.1 years; 65% female) were included, with 28.0% demonstrating low HGS and 36.8% showing low STS performance, while only 13.9% demonstrated concurrent impairments in both tests. Low SMI was observed in 25.1% of the patients. The prevalence of sarcopenia was 14.1%, frailty 23.7%, and their co-prevalence 7.2%. Conclusions: In mobility-limited older adults referred for fall assessment, sarcopenia and frailty were common conditions showing only limited overlap. The low co-prevalence between HGS and STS underscores the importance of using multiple strength assessments, while the substantial prevalence of low muscle mass highlights the need for routine muscle mass evaluation regardless of muscle strength status. Trial registration: NCT05795556

after.title: Preprint: An ICD-10-based algorithm for identifying the cause of acute respiratory failure in mechanically ventilated patients
after.authors: Kahn, J. M.; Casey, C. M.; Dsouza, J.; Martinez, S. J.; Griard, T. D.; Davis, B. S.
after.category: intensive care and critical care medicine
after.abstract: Rationale: Acute respiratory failure requiring invasive mechanical ventilation is a common reason for admission to an intensive care unit. Epidemiological research is limited by the lack of scalable approaches for identifying the primary cause of acute respiratory failure in these patients. Objective: To develop and validate an algorithm for classifying mechanically ventilated patients by the primary cause of acute respiratory failure using International Classification of Diseases, Tenth Revision (ICD-10) diagnosis and procedure codes. Methods: We identified adult patients undergoing invasive mechanical ventilation in the electronic health record of a multi-hospital health system in the United States. Using this cohort, we created a preliminary classification schema that assigned patients to one of eight mutually exclusive causes of acute respiratory failure (stroke, chronic lung disease, heart failure, trauma or overdose, pneumonia, non-pneumonia sepsis, post-operative, and other) based on the presence or absence of pre-specified ICD-10 codes. We compared the preliminary classifications to a clinical reference standard ascertained via manual chart review in a stratified random sample of the development cohort, refining the schema to optimize concordance. We then assessed content validity by examining clinical characteristics and outcomes across diagnosis categories, both in the development cohort and in an external all-payer claims dataset. Results: Of 8,130 hospitalizations in the development sample, all were successfully categorized into eight mutually exclusive groups. Compared to the reference standard of manual chart review (n=206), overall agreement was moderate (kappa = 0.44, 95% confidence interval: 0.39-0.49). After refinement, overall agreement improved slightly (kappa = 0.46, 95% confidence interval: 0.41-0.52). The final positive predictive values ranged from 78.6% (pneumonia) to 32.3% (stroke). The largest diagnostic category was non-pneumonia sepsis (26.1%), and the smallest diagnostic category was heart failure (6.2%). Clinical characteristics and outcomes approximated those expected from prior literature and were similar in the external dataset. Conclusions: A novel ICD-10-based algorithm for determining the primary cause of acute respiratory failure in patients receiving invasive mechanical ventilation was moderately accurate. This algorithm is potentially useful for facilitating large-scale epidemiological research in this population.

after.authors: Reinwald, S.; Aui, P. M.; Fettes, R. L.; Deckert, K.; Hogarth, P. M.; Hew, M.; O'Hehir, R. E.; van Zelm, M. C.
after.abstract: Background Peanut allergy is one of the most common causes of life-threatening food allergy, and therefore the focus of multiple clinical trials for allergen immunotherapy. Diagnosis relies on detection of allergen-specific serum IgE, which provides limited information on severity and threshold. Furthermore, objective biomarkers to predict allergic persistence and efficacy of treatment are lacking. Therefore, we aimed to incorporate recombinant peanut allergen components in a multiplex Cytometric Basophil detection assay (CytoBas) for detection of peanut sensitization, and in a memory B cell (Bmem) panel for evaluation of biomarkers of disease. Methods In 27 adult peanut-allergic patients, allergen-specific IgE levels were determined by ImmunoCAP, and component-specific IgE by ELISA. PBMC of all patients and of 15 non-sensitized controls were analyzed by flow cytometry with basophil markers and six fluorochrome-conjugated allergen component tetramers for CytoBas, while circulating Bmem were studied including fluorescent tetramers for Ara h 1, Ara h 2 and Ara h 3. after.title: Preprint: Modeling spontaneous hepatitis C virus clearance by age, sex, IFNL4 genotype, and infection history: Implications for simulations of elimination and vaccine trials
after.authors: Gandhi, K. R.; Mao, S.; Tatara, E.; Ozik, J.; Boodram, B.; Cotler, S. J.; Major, M.; Gutfraind, A.; Dahari, H.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Loyola University Chicago; University of Illinois Chicago
after.abstract: Background and Aims: The probability of hepatitis C virus (HCV) clearance is mediated by an interaction between numerous factors. However, variation in spontaneous HCV clearance was previously modeled using relatively simple approaches with fixed probabilities by sex. Here, we developed a literature-informed clearance algorithm that considers age, sex, interferon lambda 4 (IFNL4) genotype, and infection history to model the probability of HCV clearance in vulnerable populations, such as people who inject drugs (PWID), and in controlled human infection (CHI) models for future HCV vaccines. Methods: We modeled HCV clearance probabilities for three infection-history pathways: first infection, reinfection after spontaneous clearance, and reinfection after direct-acting antiviral (DAA) cure. Logistic and cumulative-hazard equations assigned person-specific clearance probabilities in the first two pathways. The post-DAA pathway used fixed clearance probabilities. We tested the algorithm using HepCEP (Hepatitis C Elimination in PWID), an agent-based simulator. Results: First-infection clearance probabilities ranged from 0.13 to 0.51 across eight age, sex, and IFNL4 genotype subgroups. Clearance probabilities for reinfection after spontaneous clearance ranged from 0.20 to 0.80 at literature point estimates. Across 100 runs, the mean assigned clearance probabilities were 0.27 for first infections and 0.52 for reinfections after spontaneous clearance, compared with literature inputs of 0.26 and 0.52, respectively. Probabilities varied across subgroups and runs. Conclusion: Simulations reproduced the algorithm's intended clearance heterogeneity and uncertainty by age, sex, IFNL4 genotype, and infection history, which may support models of HCV elimination in vulnerable populations and CHI model development for future HCV vaccines.

after.title: Preprint: Improving UK Biobank algorithms for Parkinson's disease ascertainment using drug claims
after.authors: Kimmerling, V.; Jaber, E.; Proust-Lima, C.; TRUONG, T.; Elbaz, A.
after.abstract: Background: Accurate ascertainment of Parkinson's disease (PD) is a major challenge in large-scale epidemiological studies. The UK Biobank (UKB) is widely used for PD research, but ascertainment based on hospital and death records may result in misclassification and delayed PD diagnoses. Objectives: We compared different strategies for ascertaining PD in the UKB, and examined their impact on incidence and associations with risk factors and mortality. Methods: We compared PD ascertained through hospital and death records (ADO-PD) to two approaches that rely on primary care data available for ~45% of participants: diagnoses from general practitioner consultations (Clinical-PD); a novel drug-based algorithm (Drug-PD). We compared incidence, age at diagnosis, and associations with sex, walking speed, and mortality across all algorithms. Results: ADO-PD identified ~20% fewer prevalent and incident cases than Drug-PD over 15y of follow-up, and estimated age at diagnosis to be 4.2y (median) later than age at anti-PD drugs initiation. ADO-PD identified never treated participants or with other causes of parkinsonism as PD patients. While Drug-PD yielded incidence rates consistent with UK reference rates, ADO-PD underestimated incidence by 36% compared to reference rates. Associations with sex, walking speed, and mortality were significantly different for ADO-PD compared to Drug-PD. Clinical-PD and Drug-PD yielded similar findings, although Clinical-PD included patients with other causes of parkinsonism. Conclusions: We draw attention to methodological issues regarding PD ascertainment in the UKB and their consequences. These results can help inform strategies for PD ascertainment by combining multiple data sources, thereby improving the validity of epidemiological analyses.

after.title: Preprint: Childhood and adolescent cancer diagnosis, treatment, and hospitalizations during the COVID-19 pandemic in Quebec, Canada, a population-based study
after.authors: Mullen, C.; Barr, R.; Coltin, H.; Strumpf, E.; El-Zein, M.; Franco, E.; Malagon, T.
after.abstract: The COVID-19 pandemic disrupted healthcare delivery globally. In Quebec, Canada, measures were introduced to prioritize pediatric oncology care. Using administrative data, we estimated pandemic-related changes in cancer diagnoses, treatments, and length of hospital stay among individuals aged 0-19 in Quebec (2015-2023). Interrupted time series analyses using autoregressive integrated moving average (ARIMA) models assessed immediate and sustained changes in monthly age-standardized rates of diagnoses, treatments (chemotherapy, surgery, radiotherapy-related encounters), positron emission tomography scans, and hospital admissions. Separate ARIMA models fitted to pre-pandemic monthly counts generated counterfactual forecasts to estimate the cumulative differences between observed and expected diagnoses and treatments over 3, 12, and 46 months of the pandemic. Generalized linear mixed models assessed changes in length of stay between the pre- and post-pandemic periods and whether these changes differed by patient characteristics. We identified 2,570 patients: 1,475 diagnosed through February 2020 and 1,095 from March 2020 onward. We found no evidence of immediate or sustained changes in monthly incidence rates. Cumulative diagnoses and treatments remained within expected levels across periods, although estimates were imprecise. For diagnoses, the 3-, 12-, and 46-month cumulative differences were -1 (95% uncertainty interval [UI] -17 to 15), 24 (95% UI, -9 to 57), and 2 (95% UI, -94 to 96), respectively. Changes in length of hospital stay varied across subgroups, although their clinical significance remains uncertain. Pediatric cancer diagnosis and treatment activity was largely maintained across Quebec throughout the pandemic, consistent with the objectives of provincial and institutional measures to preserve pediatric oncology services.

after.authors: Scott, G.; Quinn, A.; Sicard, S.; Bui, A.; Christopher, M.; Alrohaibani, A.; Kay, P.; Piche, K.; Louwrier, A.; Sandau, U.; Woltjer, R.; Quinn, J.

after.abstract: Seeded aggregation of -synuclein and tau in the gastrointestinal tract is a potential biomarker and window into disease pathogenesis, but its quantitative relationship to the brain is unknown. Here, various regions of the gut and brain from autopsies of Lewy body disease and other diagnoses were tested for seeded aggregation of -synuclein and an Alzheimer's disease-related tau species, tau-dGAE. Gut seeding of -synuclein (51.8 {+/-} 16.8 vs 112.6 {+/-} 23.0 hours) and tau-dGAE (28.5 {+/-} 2.6 vs 31.7 {+/-} 2.9 hours) was faster in Lewy body disease than non-Lewy cases and was correlated with seeding in frontal cortex and midbrain/medulla (Pearson's r from 0.75 - 0.63). Seeding of -synuclein in gut tissue was also correlated with loss of nigral pigment, pigmented neurons, Lewy bodies, and tyrosine hydroxylase-positive neurons as well as -synuclein in the dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus (r values from 0.76 - 0.49). Seeding of tau-dGAE in duodenum (but not brain) was faster in Lewy body disease compared to non-Lewy cases (28.5 {+/-} 2.6 vs 31.7 {+/-} 2.9 hours). Tau seeded aggregation in duodenum was correlated with tau-dGAE seeded aggregation in hippocampus and frontal cortex (r values from 0.58 - 0.55) and with tau and amyloid immunohistochemistry in the hippocampus, mainly for cases of Lewy body disease. Seeding for -synuclein and tau-dGAE in the gut correlated with seeding in the brain regardless of disease status. Overall data show a quantitative mirroring of peripheral and central seeded aggregation and neuropathology and demonstrate its utility for studies of pathogenesis and clinical biomarkers.

after.title: Preprint: Development and community evaluation of continuous pressure monitoring for pressure ulcer prevention and management: protocol for a mixed-methods co-design programme
after.authors: Worsley, P. R.; Aylward-Wotton, N.; Hoque, R.; Caggiari, S.; Sadler, E. A.; Kent, B.; Jiang, L.; Filingeri, D.; Duckworth, S.; Hardwick, R.; Pendray, J.; Hopper, H.; Taylor, R.; Calton, C.; Searight, C.; Lloyd, J.; Mason, V.; Tatnell, L.
after.abstract: Pressure ulcers cause substantial preventable harm, reduce quality of life and increased health and care costs. Continuous pressure monitoring (CPM) provides longitudinal information on interface pressure, posture and mobility, but evidence remains limited on its implementation, design requirements, safety and acceptability in community care. The overall aim is to develop and evaluate a theory-informed, co-produced CPM system and implementation strategy for pressure ulcer prevention and management in community settings. This sequential, theory-informed programme will comprise three linked work packages and a supporting technical-development strand. Work package 1 will use realist evaluation involving focus groups, observations and interviews to develop and refine theories explaining how CPM works, for whom and under which community circumstances. Work package 2 will use appreciative inquiry to co-produce design and implementation requirements. Technical development will integrate these requirements with mobility and pressure exposure analytics. Work package 3 is a nine-month, multisite observational mixed-methods evaluation involving 60 adults at risk of, or living with, pressure ulcers and approximately 20 carers, professionals and NHS staff across private homes, care homes and nursing homes. Outcomes will include usability, user experience, technology acceptance, feasibility, implementation, posture and mobility, pressure exposure, skin status, health-related quality of life and safety. The University of Southampton sponsors the programme, with approvals governed through the relevant UK Health Research Authority and research ethics processes. Findings will be disseminated through peer-reviewed publications, conference presentations, stakeholder networks, accessible summaries and patient and public involvement and engagement activities. This multi-site community evaluation will link evidence synthesis, programme theory, co-design, technical analytics and human-factors evaluation, to identify the conditions required for CPM to be usable, acceptable and feasible in community practice, creating the basis for a future definitive evaluation.

after.title: Preprint: The same practices, year after year: a national observational study of higher-risk antibiotic prescribing in English general practice, 2023-2026
after.authors: Agarwal, A.; Gill, A.
after.abstract: Background: There is increasing antibiotic resistance in England. National targets have been set to increase the proportion of antibiotics prescribed in the lower risk Access category. The proportion of higher risk antibiotics within the Watch+Reserve category prescribed in each general practice is publicly available. It is unclear whether a high proportion of Watch+Reserve antibiotics in a practice is due to random variation, patient population or a persistent trend. Methods: Observational study using NHS open prescribing data from 5,791 general practices in England (26.0 million items, September 2025 to August 2026, and the two previous years). Watch+Reserve proportions were compared between practices using over-dispersion adjusted funnel plots with 99.8% control limits. Practices identified as outliers were tested using subsequent data. A quasi-binomial model was fitted adjusting for age, deprivation, practice size and 7 disease registers. Results: 117 practices exceeded the 99.8% control limit (approximately 6 expected by chance). 106 practices were included in a shortlist. Of those in the shortlist in 2024/25, 61% (95% CI 52-70%) exceeded the control limit in 2025/26 compared to 1.0% of all other practices. 36 practices were shortlisted in all 3 years. Adjusting for age, deprivation, practice size and disease registers explained 4.1% of variability. Following adjustment, 101 of 106 practices remained outliers. Overall, shortlisted practices did not prescribe more antibiotics than other practices (median 422 vs 438 items per 1,000 patients per year), but did prescribe fewer Access antibiotics and more Watch+Reserve antibiotics. 10% or fewer of excess Watch+Reserve antibiotics in England were prescribed in shortlisted practices. Conclusions: A small number of practices show persistently high prescribing of higher risk antibiotics, which cannot be explained by recorded need. This provides integrated care boards (ICBs) with a reliable list of practices to review. It was not possible to investigate penicillin allergy. To meet national Access targets, interventions will be needed in all practices, particularly reviewing the use of clarithromycin, co-amoxiclav and azithromycin.

after.authors: Azimi, N.; Brian-Choux, A.; Araujo, S.; Jacob, B.; Haneda, E.; Adamy, E.; Cohen, E.; Sharon, S.; Yin, Z.; Nezami, N.; De Man, B.; Pourmorteza, A.
after.abstract: Background: Endovascular fluoroscopy provides limited depth information. Projection-level x-ray pulsing and prior-image reconstruction could enable volumetric CT updates from sparse projection data. Purpose: To assess whether pulsed sparse-view CT combined with temporally aware reconstruction could accurately localize robotically manipulated endovascular devices in a phantom. Materials and Methods: We compared true pulsed acquisitions with matched retrospective sparsification (4--180 projections) in a modular phantom. Eight robotically generated device configurations in an anthropomorphic endovascular phantom were scanned with 1248 projections. Data were retrospectively sparsified to 6, 12, 24, 32, and 52 projections and reconstructed using filtered backprojection and a temporally aware prior-image method. Localization errors were measured relative to full-view filtered-backprojection measurements. Analyses were descriptive. Results: Mean CT number differences between true pulsed and matched retrospectively sparsified images were 4.8--6.2 Hounsfield units; corrected standard deviations were 27.5--29.9 Hounsfield units. after.title: Preprint: Diffusion-based vertex-wise connectomics encodes individual differences in cognition, affect and pathology
after.authors: Pineda, J.; Cabello-Toscano, M.; Sarri, E.; Pascual-Diaz, S.; for the Alzheimer's Disease Neuroimaging Initiative,
after.abstract: No two brains are wired alike, and much of a person's cognitive and clinical state is written in this individual variation, not in the group average. Structural connectomes, however, are typically read through group atlases that summarize connectivity into regional averages, leaving this individual signal untapped. We build a vertex-wise structural connectome, in which every cortical surface vertex is a node, and apply it across the Alzheimer's continuum. Using an independent dataset for methodological development and a multisite cohort of 317 participants from ADNI-4, we show that connection distance and organizational scale form a nested hierarchy, from a long-range backbone to fine, short-range structure. The individual fingerprint is strongest in medium- and short-range connections and becomes less distinctive as connectivity is pooled into atlas parcels. This individual structure can be recovered across spatial scales, although its fidelity depends on diffusion acquisition quality, with multishell data providing a more informative reference than single-shell data. In the aging brain, an individually referenced balance between short- and long-range connectivity is associated with episodic memory, cognitive reserve, depressive symptoms, and shared molecular pathology. While cognitive associations largely reflect diagnostic differences, associations with depressive symptoms and pathology burden remain detectable after adjustment for diagnosis. These findings show that individual structural connectomes retain clinically and biologically relevant variation that is not fully captured by diagnostic classification or group-level summaries.
