after.authors: Ozakinci, G.; Schlegel, I.
after.abstract: Objective: To describe and evaluate a framework for using a large language model (LLM) as the primary coder in health content analysis, and to propose reporting items for LLM assisted studies, because no reporting standard exists. Methods: An LLM coded 6,982 Instagram and TikTok posts using a human written, human calibrated instrument. The framework has six components: human authorship of the instrument; two round human calibration; source discipline; quote anchored coding; verification in a representative and an outcome enriched sample, blinded in both directions; and per variable reliability reporting against a prespecified threshold, with the consequence of failure fixed in advance. Agreement was measured with Gwets AC1, prespecified because the outcome distribution was heavily skewed. Results: Agreement between the two human coders on the primary outcome rose from AC1 0.456 to 0.977 after two ambiguous rules were rewritten. LLM human agreement was 0.847 in the representative sample (N = 150) and 0.868 in the enriched sample (N = 50). Five of eight conditional variables fell below the 0.80 threshold and became exploratory: variables asking whether a defined textual feature was present met it, whereas those requiring graded judgement did not. The human coder identified misinformation more often than the LLM, so prevalence estimates are likely underestimates. Agreement on female targeting was lower for self-identified ethnic minority creators (0.744 versus 0.902). Conclusion: LLM coding cannot be computationally reproduced, so its reliability must be shown empirically: per variable agreement with independent human coding, the direction of remaining error, and a prespecified response to shortfall. The authors propose 18 reporting items for LLM assisted content analysis.

after.abstract: The extension of human lifespan is accompanied by a growing burden of chronic disease and multimorbidity. The immune system, whose functional state is continuously remodelled by ageing, environmental exposures, infection history and disease, is pivotal to respond to these challenges. However, how these factors jointly influence immune variation, regulatory mechanisms and disease susceptibility across populations remains poorly understood. Here we present an outline and first results of the CARDINAL (Cellular Architecture of immune-state Regulation, Disease, and Immune Networks across the Adult Lifecourse) project. We generated a new population-scale single-cell atlas of peripheral blood comprising almost 10 million immune cells from 6,003 individuals across two UK cohorts with integrated genomic and longitudinal electronic health record data: the UK Biobank (predominantly European ancestry British) and Genes & Health (British Bangladeshi and British Pakistani). We identify immune-state architectures, shared across cohorts, associated with ageing, chronic viral exposure, inflammatory activation and premalignant conditions. We show that demographic and lifestyle factors induce largely conserved immune programmes, while chronic cardiometabolic diseases are associated with cohort-dominant cellular programmes and transcriptional states. Disentangling of genetic and clinical influences reveals coordinated regulatory programmes associated with metabolic, inflammatory and infectious remodelling. These programmes are observed in specific disease contexts and immune states, such as those induced by chronic viral exposure, often independently of genetic differences. Together, our findings support a model of immune-state architecture shaped by ageing, environment, disease history and genetic variation, which can be read from population-specific regulatory landscapes.

after.abstract: Consumer wearables increasingly allow users to log cuff-measured blood pressure (BP), but resulting BP trajectories are uncharacterized. In this retrospective cohort study, 20,003 adults with Elevated BP or Stage 1 or Stage 2 Hypertension logged BP via a consumer wearable platform. We modeled 6-month trajectories with linear mixed-effects models and examined associations of [≥]5 mmHg reduction with engagement and wearable-derived metrics. Adjusted systolic reductions ranged from -2.6 mmHg (95% CI -3.1 to -2.2) in Elevated BP to -12.1 mmHg (-12.5 to -11.7) in Stage 2 Hypertension; diastolic reductions were -3.7 and -9.2 mmHg in Stage 1 and Stage 2. Overall, 50.2% achieved a [≥]5 mmHg systolic reduction and 27.9% reached normal BP. App time, journaling, AI Coach use, and BP logging were associated with higher odds of reduction; longer sleep and greater physical activity accompanied lower BP. These associational findings support consumer wearables as potentially scalable BP-monitoring platforms.

after.abstract: Background: Current diameter-based risk stratification for ascending aortic aneurysms incompletely captures patient-specific dissection risk. Here, we apply machine learning to ex vivo aortic biomechanics to define a tissue-derived risk continuum, termed aortic biomechanical vulnerability index (AortoBVI), and use magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) to predict this index in vivo. Methods: Ascending aortic tissue from 353 aneurysms, 45 normal aortas, and 46 acute aortic dissections underwent biomechanical testing. Biomechanical features were used to train a classifier distinguishing normal-like, intermediate, and dissection-like biomechanical phenotypes. Magnetic resonance imaging was performed on 38 aneurysm patients pre-operatively and 8 normal controls. Results: The classifier achieved an area under the curve (AUC) of 0.901 (95% CI 0.836-0.954). Among 38 aneurysms with pre-operative MRI, a model combining age, aortic stiffness index (ASI), and aortic pulse wave velocity (aPWV) estimated AortoBVI (R^2 = 0.580), identifying dissection-like aneurysms with an AUC of 0.928 (95% CI 0.826?0.994. These results significantly outperform aortic diameter (R^2 = 0.116, AUC 0.620). Conclusion: These findings demonstrate substantial biomechanical heterogeneity at similar aortic diameters and support biomechanics-based risk stratification of ascending aortic aneurysms.

after.authors: Fornara, E.; Hernandez, M. H.; Goday, A.; Camps-Vilaro, A.; Toledo, E.; Salas-Salvado, J.; Estruch, R.; Ros, E.; Cueto-Galan, R.; Fiol, M.; Lapetra, J.; Timiraos, J.; Serra-Majem, L.; Pinto, X.; Ruiz-Canela, M.; Vazquez-Lorente, H.; Fito, M.; Hernaez, A.
after.abstract: Background: We aimed to investigate the association between moderate-to-vigorous leisure-time physical activity (MVLTPA) and longitudinal trajectories of systolic (SBP) and diastolic (DBP) blood pressure, as well as the incidence of high blood pressure and antihypertensive drug initiation, in adults aged 60-80 years at high cardiovascular risk. Methods: In participants from the PREDIMED trial (61% women; 5,254 participants), MVLTPA was assessed using the Minnesota Leisure Time Physical Activity Questionnaire and expressed as cumulative average metabolic equivalent of task-minutes/day. SBP and DBP trajectories were modelled using mixed-effects models with cubic splines (>100 [adequate] vs <100 [insufficient] metabolic equivalent of task-minutes/day). First occurrence of high blood pressure (SBP >140 mmHg or DBP >90 mmHg) and antihypertensive drug initiation were assessed with Cox models (adequate vs insufficient, and continuous MVLTPA). Results: SBP and DBP declined with increasing age, with no clinically meaningful differences between MVLTPA groups. The association between adequate MVLTPA and incident high blood pressure was null (HR 1.11, 95% CI 0.94-1.32). However, adequate MVLTPA was associated with a 17% lower risk of antihypertensive drug initiation (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.71-0.98). The association appeared stronger in women (HR 0.74, 95% CI 0.58-0.94) than in men (HR 0.98, 95% CI 0.78-1.22) (p-value for sex interaction = 0.058). A modest inverse linear dose-response association between MVLTPA and risk of antihypertensive drug initiation was also observed (per 25 metabolic equivalent of task-minutes/day: HR 0.99, 95% CI 0.97-1.00; p-value = 0.022). Conclusions: In older adults at high cardiovascular risk, MVLTPA was not associated with clinically meaningful differences in SBP or DBP trajectories or incident high blood pressure, but was associated with a lower risk of antihypertensive drug initiation. These findings support promoting habitual physical activity as part of cardiovascular risk management in older adults.

after.abstract: Background The concurrent infection of Tuberculosis (TB) and Human Immunodeficiency Virus (HIV) constitutes a significant clinical challenge and public health emergency throughout Sub-Saharan Africa. Although national healthcare systems provide complimentary diagnostic and treatment services, early-stage mortality rates among individuals with dual infections remain critically elevated. This investigation seeks to determine independent clinical, immunological, behavioral, and geographic factors associated with mortality outcomes in TB/HIV co-infected populations within the Benoue Department of North Cameroon, employing district-level primary analytical modeling supplemented by secondary sensitivity analyses to mitigate potential bias from limited data availability. Methods A mixed retrospective and prospective cohort investigation was described, encompassing 406 co-infected individuals receiving treatment across all 14 Diagnostic and Treatment Centers (CDTs) distributed throughout the 8 health districts of the department during the period from January 1, 2022, through December 31, 2023, with extension of tuberculosis monitoring treatment ended on November 30, 2024. Statistical analysis conducted using SPSS version 25 incorporated preliminary bivariate Chi-square testing (p < 0.05) succeeded by primary multivariate binary logistic regression modeling and a supplementary sensitivity analysis stratifying geographic location into urban central versus combined peripheral and rural district categories [1-26]. Results Among 3,883 patients initiating tuberculosis treatment, 406 had concurrent HIV infection (10.46% prevalence). This co-infected group experienced significantly higher mortality at 15.02% (61/406), accounting for 84.72% (61/72) of all tuberculosis-related deaths in the department (p < 0.05). after.title: Preprint: Young peoples experiences of green social prescribing at a community farm and perceived influences on mental health and wellbeing: a qualitative study in Wales
after.authors: Wainwright, A.; Brown, M.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Swansea University College of Medicine: Swansea University Medical School
after.abstract: Mental health difficulties often begin in adolescence and early adulthood, yet most evidence on green social prescribing, which connects people with nature-based community activities to support health and wellbeing, comes from adult and quantitative research. This qualitative study explored how young people experienced taking part in a community farm programme in Wales and how they felt it influenced their mental health and wellbeing. Twelve young people aged 16 to 25 years took part in individual, semi-structured interviews at Swansea Community Farm in 2026. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis within an interpretivist paradigm. Four interconnected themes were developed:  belonging in a supportive community;  finding purpose through meaningful participation;  personal growth and enhanced wellbeing; and  nature as the context for wellbeing. Participants rarely described nature alone as responsible for feeling better. Instead, the farm brought together people who accepted them, useful work with real responsibility, and time outdoors with animals, and these were experienced together rather than separately. Participants had found the farm informally, and none had been referred through a formal social prescribing pathway. These findings suggest that green social prescribing for young people may work best when it is designed around belonging, meaningful roles and responsibility, with nature as the setting that makes these possible, and that evaluation should capture belonging, confidence and purpose as well as symptom reduction. They also point to the need for clear, youth-friendly routes into community provision, including self-referral. This was a single-site study, so it cannot show causal effects or represent the experiences of young people who did not engage, but it offers an in-depth account to inform the design and evaluation of provision for young people

after.authors: Nguyen, T.; Salama, V.; Schmidlen, J. A.; Lilly, P. M.; Wen, S.; Dunham, N.; Siochi, R. A.; Zeb, I.; Naklah, B.; Clump, D. A.; Pifer, P. M.; Hanna, M. F.
after.abstract: Background/Objectives: Cardiovascular complications following definitive chemoradiation therapy (CRT) for lung cancer are well recognized, but their longitudinal imaging manifestations remain incompletely characterized. We aimed to characterize cardiovascular abnormalities across multiple imaging modalities and electrocardiography during lung cancer survivorship. Methods: This retrospective single-center study included patients treated with definitive CRT between 2013 and 2025 who underwent baseline and follow-up cardiovascular assessments. Findings from computed tomography, echocardiography, myocardial perfusion imaging, coronary angiography, and electrocardiography were categorized into exploratory, literature-informed cardiovascular phenotype domains across five follow-up intervals. Longitudinal patterns were evaluated using generalized estimating equations (GEE). and exploratory associations with clinical cardiovascular adverse events (CVAEs) were assessed using chi-square or Fisher's exact tests. Results: Eighty-six patients were included (mean age, 66, SD=9.1 years; 46 women). Baseline coronary, thoracic aortic, and valvular calcification were common, affecting 72%, 88%, and 50% of patients, respectively. During the first 0-6 months, reduced LV systolic function (53%), valvular dysfunction (35%), and pericardial effusion (19%) were observed. Pericardial effusion was observed in 37% at 1-2 years, while calcification progression and pulmonary vascular abnormalities were identified during later follow-up intervals. Longitudinal analyses suggested positive associations between successive follow-up categories and calcification progression (average OR, 4.30), pulmonary artery enlargement (OR, 1.49; 95% CI, 1.10-2.02; P = 0.01), right-heart abnormalities (average OR, 1.65), and arrhythmia (OR, 1.76; 95% CI, 1.30-2.38; P < 0.001). Exploratory associations between imaging abnormalities and clinical CVAEs were also observed. Conclusions: Longitudinal multimodality cardiovascular assessments identified heterogeneous cardiovascular abnormalities across follow-up intervals following definitive CRT for lung cancer. Larger prospective studies are needed to validate these observations.

after.title: Preprint: Older Adults and Healthcare Professionals Perspectives on Comfort, Dignity, and Safety During Technology-Assisted Transfers: A Qualitative Descriptive Study
after.authors: Todam Nguepnang, N.; Toupin-April, K.; Karunananthan, S.; Bilodeau, M.; Jutai, J.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Interdisciplinary School of Health Sciences, Faculty of Health Sciences, University of Ottawa, Ottawa, ON, Canada
after.abstract: Purpose The experience of comfort, dignity, and safety during the use of transfer technologies remains poorly understood despite evidence supporting their effectiveness in reducing work-related musculoskeletal injuries among healthcare professionals. This study explored how older adults and healthcare professionals understand and experience comfort, dignity, and safety during technology-assisted transfers. Materials and Methods. A qualitative descriptive study guided by reflexive thematic analysis was conducted across three healthcare facilities in Ottawa, Canada. Semi-structured interviews were conducted with 15 older adults and long-term care residents requiring technology-assisted transfers, and four focus group discussions were conducted with 15 healthcare professionals. Data were analyzed using Braun and Clarke's reflexive thematic analysis. Results. Findings revealed an overarching theme: the relational nature of the transfer experience. Comfort, dignity, and safety were experienced as interconnected and reciprocal rather than as distinct outcomes. Three dimensions were identified: (1) comfort, which was physical, emotional, and relational; (2) dignity, which was restored through how staff treated the person; and (3) safety, which depended on trust in the person operating the device and, for professionals, on clinical judgment and adaptability. Participants also highlighted the importance of staff training, equipment customization, communication, and adequate staffing to enhance transfer experiences. Conclusion. Comfort, dignity, and safety during technology-assisted transfers are not inherent properties of transfer devices but are co-constructed through interactions among older adults, healthcare professionals, and technologies. Transfer quality depended on relational practices, such as communication, privacy, and staff continuity, alongside technical competence. Training that combines technical and relational skills, stable staffing, and adaptable equipment may improve transfer experiences. Keywords: assistive technology; patient transfer; comfort; dignity; safety; older adults; long-term care; person-centred care

after.abstract: Objective: Ro52/TRIM21 is a cytoplasmic protein that binds intracellular antibodies and drives their proteasomal degradation. Autoantibodies targeting Ro52 frequently co-occur with myositis-specific autoantibodies, including anti-MDA5, and patients with both autoantibodies have greater disease severity and interstitial lung disease risk. We previously demonstrated that internalized anti-MDA5 autoantibodies promote interferon-stimulated gene expression in cultured myoblasts. Here, we investigated the interactions between anti-Ro52 and coexisting autoantibodies, including anti-MDA5. Methods: Primary human skeletal muscle myoblasts were electroporated with purified IgG from healthy controls or patients with anti-MDA5, anti-Mi-2, or anti-PM/Scl antibodies, combined with anti-Ro52-positive IgG from patients with myositis, Sjogren's disease, or systemic sclerosis. Affinity-purified anti-Ro52 was also used to validate findings obtained using total IgG. Cells underwent bulk RNA sequencing 24 hours after internalization. Results: Co-internalization of anti-Ro52 with anti-MDA5 enhanced the anti-MDA5-induced type I interferon transcriptional response and expression of type II interferon-inducible genes compared with anti-MDA5 and control IgG. Increased expression of IFNB1, ISG15, MX1, and the interferon-g-inducible inflammatory chemokines CXCL9 and CXCL10 was observed across independent patient-derived antibody combinations, anti-Ro52 preparations from multiple autoimmune diseases, and affinity-purified anti-Ro52. Conversely, co-internalization of anti-Ro52 with anti-Mi-2 or anti-PM/Scl reduced expression of transcripts associated with these nuclear autoantibodies. Conclusions: These findings demonstrate that anti-Ro52 autoantibodies potentiate the activation of interferon pathways stimulated by the internalization of anti-MDA5 antibodies. We propose that in patients with anti-MDA5 autoantibodies, co-existing anti-Ro52 antibodies may exacerbate disease by inhibiting the proteasomal degradation of internalized anti-MDA5 antibodies and thereby enhancing the expression of interferon and interferon-stimulated genes.

after.abstract: Background Cervical cancer remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in low- and middle-income countries, particularly among women living with HIV (WLHIV). Although visual-based assessment in primary care is feasible and facilitates same-day management, its diagnostic accuracy is dependent on provider experience and skill, resulting in variable performance. Portable gynecological imaging may enhance visual assessment while supporting implementation of cervical cancer prevention in primary care. Methods We will conduct a cross-sectional study among 150 WLHIV co-infected with human papillomavirus and their healthcare providers at Molo Sub-County Hospital in Nakuru County, Kenya. The study will evaluate the agreement between portable gynecological imaging-enhanced visual assessment and conventional colposcopy; estimate diagnostic accuracy using histopathology as the reference standard; determine provider-level acceptability, appropriateness, and feasibility, and assess patient-level satisfaction using validated instruments complemented by qualitative interviews and integrated using a sequential, explanatory, mixed-methods approach. Discussion This study will generate preliminary evidence on the diagnostic accuracy and implementation of portable gynecological imaging in primary care. If shown to be accurate, acceptable, appropriate, and feasible, portable gynecological imaging could improve timely identification and management of cervical precancer, and support expansion of high-quality cervical cancer prevention services in similar resource-limited settings.

after.abstract: Time-restricted eating (TRE) is a promising strategy to improve weight management and metabolic health, but its efficacy may vary depending on the coherence between the eating window and individual chronotype. In a randomized 12-week intervention of morning chronotype adults with overweight or obesity, early TRE (06:00h-14:00h) led to greater reductions in body fat mass compared to late TRE (12:00h-20:00h) and active control (three meals per day). Continuous glucose monitoring revealed enhanced circadian glucose rhythmicity and increased glycemic variability in early TRE, whereas postprandial glucose excursions were attenuated in late TRE. Early TRE induced the most pronounced systemic multi-omic changes, characterized by distinct transcriptional and metabolic programs, including reduced triglyceride and increased sphingomyelin levels. We found that in morning chronotype, early TRE and late TRE elicit distinct adaptations in body composition, glucose and lipid metabolism, and altered transcriptional and metabolic signatures. ClinicalTrials.gov registration no. NCT04618133.

after.abstract: Background: Maternal body mass index (BMI) [≥]30kg/m2 has previously been associated with reduced infant neurocognitive development, including educational attainment. The mechanistic pathway underlying this association is unclear. Objective: We examined the relationship between observed maternal BMI, maternal genetic liability for BMI, and infant mid-childhood educational attainment. We aimed to limit residual confounding by environmental factors, for example socioeconomic status. Methods: A BMI polygenic risk score (PRSBMI) was applied to eligible participants in the Pregnancy Outcome Prediction study (n=2437). Six educational outcomes through mid-childhood (age 5, age 6, and 4 domains at age 7) were regressed on (i) maternal pre-pregnancy BMI based on self-reported weight (ii) maternal PRSBMI and (iii) residual BMI unexplained by PRSBMI. Participants were stratified into four risk groups by PRSBMI risk and observed BMI. Relationships between each risk group and educational outcomes were examined. All association analyses were adjusted for confounders including school funding type, socioeconomic status, and serious childhood morbidity. Causality was evaluated using two-sample Mendelian randomisation (MR). False discovery rate (FDR) was controlled using the Benjamini-Hochsberg correction at alpha=0.05. after.authors: Ochola, H.; Atukunda, E. C.; Atuhumuza, E. B.; Haberer, J.; Nghiem, V. T.; Waiswa, P.; Kanyesigye, M.; Tibaijuka, L.; Lugaaju, C.; Asasira, J.; Turanzomwe, S.; Obua, C.; Siedner, M. J.; Matthews, L. T.; Mugyenyi, G. R.

after.abstract: Social support during pregnancy can influence women's engagement with antenatal care and other maternal health behaviours. Maternal health programmes in sub-Saharan Africa have often emphasised male partner involvement, although women may draw on broader social networks. Evidence on whom women identify as their primary supporter during pregnancy remains limited. We examined the prevalence and factors associated with non-spousal primary supporter selection among pregnant women in southwestern Uganda. We conducted a cross-sectional analysis of baseline data from the Support-Moms study, a Type 1 hybrid effectiveness-implementation randomised controlled trial conducted in Mbarara City, Mbarara District, and Mitooma District, southwestern Uganda. Pregnant women enrolled between 27 February and 17 December 2024 identified two social supporters before randomisation; the first-nominated individual was classified as the primary supporter. The primary outcome was selection of a non-spousal primary supporter. Modified Poisson regression with robust variance was used to estimate crude and adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs) with 95% confidence intervals (CIs). Among 824 women, 223 (27.1%; 95% CI 24.1-30.3) selected a non-spousal primary supporter. Friends (30.5%) and other relatives (28.7%) were the most frequently nominated non-spousal supporters, followed by siblings (17.9%) and mothers (16.6%). Non-spousal selection was more prevalent among women recruited in Mbarara District (aPR 1.50, 95% CI 1.09-2.08) and Mitooma District (aPR 2.52, 95% CI 1.77-3.60) than Mbarara City, and among women who were separated, divorced, widowed, or never married (aPR 2.35, 95% CI 1.76-3.14), had an unplanned pregnancy (aPR 1.39, 95% CI 1.10-1.77), had a >10-year relationship with their nominated supporter (aPR 1.93, 95% CI 1.39-2.69), or were aged <20 years (aPR 1.48, 95% CI 1.01-2.15). Although spouses were the primary supporters for most women, more than one-quarter nominated someone else, most commonly a friend or relative. These findings suggest that pregnancy support extends beyond marital relationships and may be shaped by relational status, social context, pregnancy intention, age, and established social ties. Antenatal care programmes may benefit from complementing partner-focused approaches with mechanisms to engage other support figures identified by women.

after.authors: Temesgen, S. N.; Ayele, F. A.; Tabor, T. E.; Alemayehu, B. A.; Beze, G. A.
after.author_corresponding_institution: University of Gondar College of Medicine and Health Sciences
after.abstract: Glaucoma is a chronic illness that can create a significant financial burden for patients. A hospital-based cross-sectional study was conducted to assess the economic burden of glaucoma among patients at the University of Gondar Tertiary Eye Care and Training Centre. Consecutive sampling was used, and 325 patients who had taken antiglaucoma medication for at least six months participated in the study. Data were collected using a structured questionnaire; after a proper checkup, the data were entered into EpiData version 4.7 and exported to Stata version 17 for further analysis. Descriptive statistics, bivariate screening, and final multiple linear regression after log transformation were performed to assess outcome variables as well as the relationship between the total cost and independent variables. The mean age of the participants was 61 (range: 18-90). Males accounted for 60.31%. The most common type of glaucoma was POAG, which accounted for 67.38%, followed by pseudoexfoliative glaucoma (12.92%). The mean total cost related to glaucoma management per patient in this study was 904.75 ETB (5.86 USD) monthly. This constituted 22.1% of the participants' mean monthly income. Total cost related to glaucoma was significantly associated with residency, health insurance coverage, laterality of the disease, number of anti-glaucoma medications, and history of glaucoma surgery. The study revealed that glaucoma had a significant effect on patients economic, personal, and social quality of life. It is recommended to expand the community-based health insurance system to include those anti-glaucoma drugs bought from private pharmacies.

after.title: Preprint: Descriptive Histomorphology of Palatine Tonsils Among Children Undergoing Tonsillectomy at a Zonal Referral Hospital in Dar es Salaam, Tanzania
after.authors: Kihanda, J.; Nnyiti, N.; Karua, P.; Russa, D.
after.abstract: Background: Palatine tonsils play a critical role in paediatric immune function, with their microarchitecture influencing susceptibility to disease. Despite the burden of tonsillar diseases in Tanzania, limited data exist on local histomorphological patterns that may underpin disease mechanisms. This study was conducted to evaluate the histomorphological characteristics of palatine tonsils in children undergoing tonsillectomy at a zonal referral hospital in Dar es Salaam. Materials and Methods: This descriptive cross-sectional study analysed 86 tonsillectomy specimens collected from children aged [≤]15 years between March and May 2025. Gross morphology (weight, surface, consistency) and histological features (epithelial thickness, crypt density, and high endothelial venule [HEV] density) were assessed using H&E staining and digital image analysis. Statistical analysis was performed using SPSS v20, with significance set at p < 0.05. Results: Tonsillar hypertrophy was the most common surgical indication (54.7%). Heavier tonsils and smooth, soft surfaces were significantly associated with hypertrophy (p < 0.001), whereas recurrent tonsillitis correlated with irregular, firm tonsils. Surface epithelium was thicker than crypt epithelium (14{+/-}3 vs. 12{+/-}2 cell layers) and HEV density was higher in the surface epithelium (2.01{+/-}0.63 vs. 1.55{+/-}0.58/high power field). No statistically significant differences in epithelial thickness, crypt number, or HEV distribution were observed between clinical groups. Conclusion: The study demonstrated conserved histological features across clinical groups with subtle tissue remodelling in disease states, suggesting that immunological and molecular responses may underlie the mechanisms of tonsillar disease in this population.

after.authors: Li, M.; Yang, Y.; Shen, L.; Ping, J.; Jia, G.; Fang, H.; Long, J.; Schiemann, W.; Tang, H.; Zheng, W.; Zhu, X.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Population and Quantitative Health Sciences, Case Western Reserve University School of Medicine, Cleveland, OH, USA
after.abstract: Most breast cancer (BC) risk loci identified by genome wide association studies lie in noncoding regions, and traditional transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) often prioritize multiple correlated genes per locus. We applied two gene fine-mapping methods, TGVIS and M cTWAS, which jointly model gene expression, splicing and alternative polyadenylation (APA) with direct variant effects, to overall BC, estrogen receptor-negative (ER negative) BC and triple-negative BC (TNBC) in women of European and African ancestry. Using 11 BC-relevant GTEx v10 tissues, we prioritized 31, 13 and 5 candidate causal genes, respectively, in European-ancestry populations. Compared with marginal TWAS, fine-mapping reduced the number of candidate genes per locus by 72 to 88%, and credible sets explained 97 to 100% of significant marginal associations. Seven candidates were not reported by previous GTEx v8-based TWAS, including RIN3, supported only by APA, and NPAT for TNBC. Analyses across 48 tissues and brain cell types revealed brain contributions, including ARHGEF5 in oligodendrocytes. In African-ancestry populations, EN1 was prioritized for ER negative BC and TNBC through variants common in African but rare in European ancestry. These results refine BC susceptibility genes, highlight regulatory mechanisms beyond breast tissue and gene expression, and reveal the challenge of mapping GWAS variants to causal genes with currently available data.

after.authors: Lau, Y.; Cooper, C.; Dobson, R.; Banerjee, S.; Demnitz-King, H.
after.abstract: Background: Dementia and frailty frequently coexist, and each increases hospitalisation and mortality risk. We examined frailty prevalence among people with dementia in England, and whether its associations with hospitalisation and mortality differ from those in people without dementia. Methods: Using Clinical Practice Research Datalink primary care data linked to hospital and mortality records, we matched people with dementia to controls by year of birth, sex, and practice, and measured frailty using the electronic Frailty Index. We modelled hospitalisation episodes and total bed days and mortality, and tested effect modification by ethnicity, deprivation, and rurality. Results: In 2021, 58.1% of people with dementia were living with frailty, compared with 29.4% in controls. In outcome analyses (556,685 people with dementia and 1,526,612 controls), among people with dementia, severe versus no frailty was associated with more hospitalisation episodes (aIRR 1.47, 95% CI 1.45,1.50) and higher mortality (aHR 1.58, 1.54,1.62). Mild and moderate frailty were associated with slightly fewer bed days (aIRR 0.96, 0.95,0.97; 0.99, 0.97,0.99) and severe frailty with more (aIRR 1.04, 1.01,1.07). Associations were stronger among controls (severe frailty: episodes aIRR 3.07, 2.99,3.14; bed days 3.28, 3.17,3.38; mortality aHR 2.74, 2.66,2.82). Conclusions: Frailty is common among people with dementia and associated with more hospital admissions and higher mortality. Its relationship with bed days is more complex, possibly reflecting difficulties discharging people with dementia home rather than to residential care. Frailty assessment and management should be a core part of dementia care.

after.title: Preprint: An LLM-assisted Pipeline for Identifying ClinicalTrials.gov Registry Changes and Their Association with Primary Endpoint Positivity
after.authors: Purevdorj, A.; Dennstaedt, F.; Zwahlen, D. R.; Windisch, P.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Department of Radiation Oncology, Cantonal Hospital Winterthur, Winterthur, Switzerland
after.abstract: Registration of randomized clinical trials (RCTs) in a public registry such as ClinicalTrials.gov should minimize the risk of reporting bias. However, records may be modified during a trial and the resulting discrepancies are not always apparent without a detailed examination of all version histories, a process that is cumbersome when performed manually. We developed an automated workflow to investigate whether specific changes to RCT registry entries are associated with primary endpoint positivity. Our pipeline extracts RCT records from ClinicalTrials.gov and systematically detects changes between successive versions using a combination of deterministic textual analysis and large language model (LLM)-assisted classification. We could show a positive association between trial positivity and changes to primary outcomes (OR 1.91; 95% CI 1.48-2.47) as well as to arms and interventions (OR 2.10; 95% CI 1.62-2.73). Associations were weaker when changes occurred exclusively before the primary completion date, pointing to the importance of timing in evaluating potentially consequential modifications to RCT design. Our automated pipeline can enable analysis of trial registration records at scale, facilitating the work of reviewers and meta-scientists to promote research integrity.

after.authors: Xu, J.; Zhang, W.; Yuan, Y.; Wu, C.
after.author_corresponding_institution: The University of Texas MD Anderson Cancer Center
after.abstract: Predicting clinical trial outcomes requires interpreting biological and clinical evidence in the context of a specific intervention, population and study design. Here we test whether a general-purpose large language model (LLM) can predict trial outcomes from publicly available evidence. We introduce TrialDossier, which assembles standardized evidence dossiers, and TrialOutlook, which uses these dossiers with GPT-5 to estimate the probability that a trial meets its prespecified primary endpoint. Among 694 ongoing trials with results expected within six months of cohort assembly, 69 outcomes first disclosed after forecast recording had been adjudicated by 20 October 2026. TrialOutlook achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.819 (95% confidence interval, 0.708 to 0.914) and an average precision of 0.860. TrialOutlook correctly identified 27 of 29 failures (93.1%) and incorrectly classified 17 of 40 successes as failures. We further recorded forecasts for 5,809 ongoing trials associated with US-listed companies and established a public benchmark linking archived evidence and fixed forecasts to adjudicated outcomes as they become available.

after.title: Preprint: ADSMoE: A mixture-of-experts-based transformer autoencoder for discovering multimodal Alzheimer's disease subtypes
after.authors: Meng, W.; Pan, J.; Yin, M.; Zhuang, P.; Gong, K.; Lin, M.; Xu, J.; Burns, M.; Wu, Y.; Yin, R.
after.abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) exhibits substantial biological and clinical heterogeneity, posing critical challenges for advancing precision medicine. Existing data-driven approaches often rely on modality-specific clustering or predefined biomarker trajectories, limiting their ability to discover disease subtypes from incomplete, heterogeneous real-world data. In this study, we introduce ADSMoE, a mixture-of-experts (MoE)-based multimodal representation learning framework that jointly identifies AD subtypes as latent disease signatures while accommodating incomplete modality combinations. ADSMoE integrates a Fleximodal MoE encoder that accommodates arbitrary combinations of available modalities with a novel subtype-specific MoE decoder to capture complementary disease characteristics through expert specialization. Using data from 5,422 participants across three independent cohorts, we trained ADSMoE on the ADNI cohort and externally validated the identified subtypes in NACC and UKB without model retraining. The proposed ADSMoE identified four AD subtypes with distinct neuroimaging patterns, genetic and proteomic associations, and clinical characteristics. Benchmarking analyses demonstrated robust subtype discovery and strong biological and clinical relevance, while external validation revealed consistent subtype-associated characteristics across independent cohorts. ADSMoE advances AD subtyping by uncovering biologically and clinically meaningful AD heterogeneity from incomplete multimodal data, providing a scalable framework for disease stratification, biomarker discovery, and future precision medicine applications in AD.

after.title: Preprint: Long-term transmission chains fueling the drug-resistant tuberculosis burden in Southern Brazil
after.authors: Soares, T. d. S.; Pivato, A. F.; Frosi, F.; Pavanelo, D. B.; Godinho, F.; Minghelli, S.; de David, S.; Bello, G. L.; Walter, K.; Perdigao, J.; Ramis, I.; da Silva, P. E. A.; Salvato, R. S.
after.author_corresponding_institution: Departamento de Analises Clinicas, Bromatologicas e Toxicologicas, Faculdade de Ciencias Farmaceuticas de Ribeirao Preto, Universidade de Sao Paulo, Ribeirao Pr
after.abstract: Background Tuberculosis (TB) remains a leading infectious cause of death, with drug-resistant TB (DR-TB) challenging disease control. Brazil has a high TB burden, and Rio Grande do Sul state reports persistently high incidence and drug-resistance rates. The drivers shaping the regional DR-TB burden remain poorly characterised. Methods We conducted genomic surveillance of confirmed DR-TB cases in Rio Grande do Sul, Brazil, from January 2023 to September 2024. Clinical isolates underwent genotypic (gDST) and phenotypic drug susceptibility testing (pDST) and whole-genome sequencing (WGS). We analyzed 33 newly sequenced genomes and 267 historical Mycobacterium tuberculosis genomes collected in 2011-2019 to characterize resistance, transmission, and spatiotemporal patterns and estimate the contributions of transmitted and acquired rifampicin resistance. Findings Molecular testing detected rifampicin resistance missed by pDST, including borderline rpoB mutations in 18.2% and emerging resistance-associated variants in 3% of the 33 analyzed isolates. Conversely, pDST detected baseline bedaquiline resistance missed by WGS in one newly diagnosed case. Among 300 genomes, 181 (60.3%) clustered into 32 genomic clusters at a 5-SNP threshold, including 12 with long-term circulation and several spanning prisons and communities. Sublineage frequencies remained stable over time, whereas we observed marked geographic structuring and localized clonal expansion. Among 178 rifampicin-resistant isolates, transmission accounted for an estimated 79.2-88.2% of resistance, corresponding to 11.8-20.8% of cases arising through de novo acquisition during treatment. Interpretation Our findings identify active transmission as the main driver of rifampicin-resistant TB in Rio Grande do Sul, with long-term transmission chains extending across both incarcerated and community settings. These results underscore the urgent need to strengthen timely TB case detection and resistance testing, enhance contact investigations, and implement targeted interventions aiming to interrupt persistent transmission chains.

after.title: Preprint: Two Axes of Sleep, One Heart: Dissociating Objective Sleep-Disordered Breathing From Subjective Sleep Duration in Cardiac Risk
after.authors: Deng, Q.; Ma, N.; Aan, T.; Pang, D.
after.abstract: Background: Cardiovascular epidemiology has long treated "sleep" as a single exposure, although it denotes both an objective physiological state and a subjective behaviour. We tested whether these domains carry separable information about cardiac risk. Methods and Results: We derived an objective axis from 8,444 polysomnograms (Sleep Heart Health Study) and a subjective axis of self-reported duration from 407,303 adults in the 2020 and 2022 Behavioral Risk Factor Surveillance System. Multivariable regression (n=213,489), quadratic dose-response modelling, sleep-stratified comorbidity networks, and era-stratified tests were combined. Objective sleep-disordered breathing was continuous and right-skewed (median apnea-hypopnea index, 31.8 events/h; median sleep efficiency, 69%) in a risk-enriched cohort. Both short (<7 h) and long (>9 h) sleep were associated with disease after full adjustment: adjusted odds ratios for heart attack were 1.24 (95% CI, 1.19-1.30) and 1.30 (1.19-1.42), and for stroke 1.12 (1.06-1.17) and 1.42 (1.29-1.57). A positive quadratic term confirmed a U shape for all 4 outcomes formally tested (P[≤]6.3x102), with fitted nadirs of 7.26 to 7.85 hours. Suboptimal sleep also raised comorbidity-network density from 0.089 to 0.112 (short sleep; +26%) and 0.108 (long sleep; +22%), with non-overlapping bootstrap CIs and concordant effects across demographic strata. A survey-weighted replication in official CDC microdata (n=344,010; median design effect, 4.43) preserved the principal cardiac, U-shaped, and network findings; an exploratory COVID-19 interaction (P=0.020) did not survive design-based correction. Conclusions: Objective breathing pathology and subjective duration are separately prognostic, and suboptimal sleep amplifies the cardiometabolic comorbidity network. Duration alone cannot exclude asymptomatic sleep-disordered breathing; cardiovascular prevention should assess both axes.

after.title: Preprint: Kidney Function Variability and Cardiovascular Outcomes in Heart Failure: Effects of Empagliflozin in the EMPEROR-Reduced Trial
after.authors: Kunitake, M.; Higuchi, K.; Sakai, Y.; Fukumoto, Y.
after.abstract: Background: Although sodium-glucose cotransporter-2 (SGLT2) inhibitors improve cardiovascular and kidney outcomes in patients with heart failure (HF), the prognostic significance of intraindividual kidney function variability and its modification by SGLT2 inhibition remain unclear. We investigated these relationships in patients with HF with reduced ejection fraction (HFrEF). Methods: This secondary analysis included 3,492 patients from the EMPEROR-Reduced trial. A location-scale joint model (LSJM) simultaneously evaluated the associations of estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) levels, longitudinal slopes, and intraindividual variability from day 28 onward with the composite outcome of cardiovascular death or HF hospitalization. Patients were stratified into tertiles of estimated eGFR variability using common cutoffs across the empagliflozin and placebo groups, allowing comparisons of cardiovascular outcomes at comparable variability levels. Results: Greater intraindividual eGFR variability was independently associated with increased cardiovascular risk (hazard ratio: 1.08 per 1 mL/min/1.73 m2 increase in estimated standard deviation; P < 0.001). The model incorporating eGFR levels, slopes, and variability demonstrated the best fit. Empagliflozin significantly reduced eGFR variability compared with placebo (standard deviation ratio: 0.93; P = 0.005) and attenuated annual eGFR decline by 1.83 mL/min/1.73 m2/year, despite an initial eGFR reduction of approximately 2.5 mL/min/1.73 m2. Event-free survival progressively decreased with increasing eGFR variability in both treatment groups. Importantly, within each variability tertile defined by common cutoffs, empagliflozin-treated patients consistently exhibited higher event-free survival than placebo-treated patients. Conclusion: In patients with HFrEF, greater intraindividual eGFR variability was independently associated with adverse cardiovascular outcomes, beyond eGFR levels and slopes. Empagliflozin reduced kidney function variability and attenuated long-term eGFR decline, with more favorable cardiovascular outcomes observed even among patients with comparable levels of kidney function variability.

after.authors: Hishman, A. O.; Taabe, D.; Boateng, J. O.; Kusi, K. A.; Besah Sorvor, F. K. A.; Twumasi, E. A.; Amoateng, A. F.; Amenu, J.; Wiredu, O. K.; Mensah, E. B.; Saaiby, A. S.; Akoto, B. O.; Kwarteng, E. O.; Cappello, M.; Brenya, P. K.
after.abstract: Background: Tuberculosis remains a major public health challenge in Ghana, where GeneXpert MTB/RIF serves as a first-line diagnostic tool. However, uncertainties about this method persist regarding specimen quality and the clinical significance of indeterminate rifampicin susceptibility results. Methods: We conducted a retrospective cross-sectional study of samples from 3,977 presumptive TB patients tested either at HopeXchange Medical Center (Kumasi) or Keta Municipal Hospital between January 2020 and December 2024. Demographic data, sputum macroscopic appearance, and GeneXpert results were analyzed using descriptive statistics and Fishers exact test. Results: Overall Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTb) test positivity was 11.6% (461/3977). Males accounted for 63.3% of positive results, with the highest percentage among those ages 30-40 years. Mucopurulent specimens yielded the highest positivity rate (25.4%), compared to 4.0% of salivary specimens. Blood-stained sputum specimens (n=44) showed a 15.9% positivity rate. Although confirmed rifampicin resistance was low (1.7%), 9.3% of all MTb positive samples yielded an indeterminate result. The rate of indeterminate results from samples collected at Kwadaso Municipal increased from 7.3% in 2021 to 28.6% in 2024. Conclusion: These findings validate Ghana National Tuberculosis Program (NTP) guidelines emphasizing the reliability of mucopurulent specimen collection, but challenges the routine rejection of blood-stained sputum. The rising trend of indeterminate rifampicin results requires further investigation of circulating rpoB mutation profiles and quality assurance measures. Patients with indeterminate results should be further assessed using drug susceptibility testing to rule out rifampicin resistance. The findings provide actionable evidence to refine diagnostic algorithms and improve TB care in Ghana.

after.title: Preprint: The Interplay Between Sex, Rater, and Autism Polygenic Scores on Autistic Traits in General Population Adolescents
after.authors: Sollie, T.; de Wit, M. M.; Pool, R.; Autism Working Group of the Psychiatric Genomics Consortium,  ; Bartels, M.; Polderman, T. J.; Akingbuwa, W. A.
after.abstract: Autism is diagnosed more often in males than in females, but it remains unclear to what extent this reflects sex differences in autistic traits themselves or in how those traits are recognised. We compare up to four raters of the same participants, testing whether autistic trait scores differ by sex across raters, and whether the association with autism polygenic scores (PGS) differs by sex (genetic sex amplification) or rater. We derived autistic trait scores from mother- (n = 4,541), father- (n = 3,674), teacher- (n = 2,939), and self-reports (n = 2,632) on an autism subscale of the Achenbach System of Empirically Based Assessment (ASEBA) for 12-14-year-olds in the Young Netherlands Twin Register (total n = 6,163). Ordinal mixed-effects regression modelled a three-way interaction between PGS, rater, and sex. Measurement invariance analysis tested the subscale items for sex bias. Mothers, fathers, and teachers rated males higher than females (odds ratios (OR) = 1.56, 1.49, and 2.34), whereas females rated themselves higher than males did (OR = 0.71, males as reference). Autism PGS were associated with higher autistic trait scores (OR = 1.22), but this association did not differ by rater or sex. One item ("Acts too young for his/her age") was biased towards males in mother- and self-ratings. These rater effects are consistent with under-recognition of autistic traits in females by external raters. In contrast, the PGS association did not differ by sex or rater, providing no evidence for sex amplification, though current autism PGS have limited predictive power.

after.title: Preprint: Intimate partner violence victimization and perpetration with greater probability of brain injury in victims: A preliminary study
after.authors: Adhikari, S. P.; McLennan, C.; Rothlander, K.; Mason, K.; van Donkelaar, P.
after.abstract: Background: Intimate Partner Violence (IPV) can be either unidirectional or bidirectional. At times when it is bidirectional, the impact of the IPV would likely be greater in women compared to men especially in cases involving physical IPV. This study compared IPV victimization and perpetration characteristics and explored the relationship between IPV victimization and brain injury (BI) among women victims of IPV. Methods: In this cross-sectional study, 23 women (IPV victims) aged 18-60 years who experienced at least one reported incident of IPV-BI were recruited from different community-based, women-serving organizations. Data collection included a comprehensive assessment of IPV, BI, and psychopathological comorbidities. The Conflict Tactics Scale-2 (CTS2) was used to assess for victimization and perpetration. Results: The participants had significantly lower scores on the physical assaults (t = 5.94, p < 0.0001, p2 = 0.62), and higher scores on the injury (t = 6.12, p < 0.001, p2 = 0.63) domains of the CTS2 compared to the perpetrator/partner. The physical assault scores of the perpetrator/partner were significantly correlated with the injury scores of the victim (r = 0.86, p < 0.001). Moreover, victims injury scores and their BISA scores were also significantly correlated (r = 0.69, p = 0.002). Conclusions: Women victims of IPV, in contrast to perpetrator/partners, demonstrated greater physical injury, which were associated with an increased likelihood of BI in this cohort. Findings should be interpreted cautiously, as partners data were based on victim reports. Further studies are warranted to explore the possible occurrence of BI in perpetrators and then directly compare the injury exposure in victims versus perpetrators. Based on the findings of this study, it is clear there is a higher prevalence, as well as greater exposure, of BI and more serious consequences of IPV and/or IPV-BI on victims compared to that of perpetrators.
